Fix the prices offline, re-import, and the application shows every change field by field before writing anything. No more 124 dialogs when a provider revises its grid.
items.i2: 🛡️ An import cannot break the catalogue — a row missing from the file never deletes anything: a forgotten Excel filter cannot empty your catalogue, and a removal is declared explicitly through an "active" column. The import is all-or-nothing: any problem is reported with the sheet and the cell to fix, and nothing is written. If a model changed between the preview and the confirmation, only the affected rows are refused — not the whole file.
items.i3: 💶 Two billing errors fixed — a dated model that owns its own tariff was billed at its base model's price (gpt-4o-2024-05-13 counted 2.50 instead of 5.00 on input), and two read paths could return different prices for the same model at the same instant. Both are repaired, and a database constraint stops the second from coming back. The workbook also states in words which models are billed zero for lack of an active tariff, and shows time-slot pricing on the row that carries the price.
items.i4: 🔌 A deactivated model can be switched back on — deactivation had no inverse in the application. A retired model is now reactivated from the workbook, and a cached-input price can finally be cleared rather than endured.

v1_30_10.title: v1.30.10 — 🧭 Your capabilities, up to date and on every card

items.i1: ✨ The capability map finally shows everything LIA can do — image generation, document generation, plugins, learned habits, your MCP servers and phone calls were all missing from “Capabilities”: the page whose whole job is to be current had quietly fallen a few releases behind. It now maps nineteen capabilities instead of thirteen, and a capability an administrator switches off disappears from it immediately instead of being announced as available.
items.i2: 🧭 The settings home page now says where each section stands — “Memory — active, 128 items”, “Connectors — to set up”: every section that holds something says so on its card, before you open it. The whole page reads it in a single request, and stays silent rather than guessing while the answer is on its way or when a section has nothing to report.
items.i3: 🧩 MCP servers move in with the other extensions — “Application MCP” and “MCP servers” leave Preferences and join Features › Extensions & Data, beside Skills, Plugins and Spaces: a server that hands the assistant new tools extends it, where a connector links a personal account. Your existing links keep working. The FAQ also gains a Plugins section, and its settings instructions now describe the page as it actually is.
items.i4: 🆕 The public site shows what just shipped — the latest releases are now told in plain words on the home page, with the full history one click away. Visitors can see the product moving before they even create an account.

v1_30_9.title: v1.30.9 — 🧭 Settings, redesigned: everything one click away

items.i1: 🧭 A modern master-detail settings page — settings are no longer a wall of collapsed lists: a permanent side rail shows every section, grouped and iconed, and the chosen section opens fully in a panel beside it. With nothing selected, an overview presents every setting as a card with its description — finally visible before you open anything. On the phone, the list comes first and each section opens full screen with a back button.
items.i2: 🔎 Search now covers administration, and section links can be shared — administrators find every admin panel (users, pricing, LLM configuration…) through the same quick search, and every section has a stable address: reload or share the URL and you land exactly there. If a section isn't available on your account, the page says so plainly — and keeps watching, in case it simply took time to load.
items.i3: 📄 Generated documents open in the app — click a document card and it opens in a viewer tab: CSV as a real table, Markdown and text nicely rendered; Word, Excel and PowerPoint present a clean download panel, and PDFs keep opening straight in the browser.

v1_30_8.title: v1.30.8 — 📄 Document generation: real files, on demand

items.i1: 📄 Ask for a real document, get a real file — LIA now writes complete documents on demand: CSV and Excel spreadsheets, Word reports, PowerPoint presentations, PDF, Markdown and plain text. Ask in the chat (“research the latest LLM models and turn it into a CSV”, “make a detailed presentation about Alsace”) and the finished file appears as a downloadable card below the answer — it can chain directly on a web research done in the same request. A dedicated writer model produces the content in your language; spreadsheets are safe by construction (no formula injection) and Excel-ready.
items.i2: 🕒 Files that say when they expire — every generated document card shows its filename, its size and its exact expiry deadline; PDFs open right in a browser tab, everything else downloads in one click. Generation is switchable instance-wide by the administrator and covered by the same usage limits as the rest of your AI usage.

v1_30_7.title: v1.30.7 — 🧩 Agent Plugins: install portable plugins

items.i1: 🧩 Install plugins from the whole AI ecosystem — LIA speaks the open Agent Plugins standard (agent-plugins.org, backed by AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, Cursor and Vercel). A plugin packaged for ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or VS Code installs into LIA unchanged, from a zip file or an https link, and brings its skills and MCP servers in one step. Every install shows a full report — what was installed, updated, skipped (and why) or removed — and uninstalling removes everything the plugin brought, in one action. New “Plugins” section in Settings, in all six languages.
items.i2: 🧹 Account deletion now removes every skill and plugin file — deleting your account already purged your data from the database; it now also removes your imported skill files and installed plugin files from disk, completing the clean-slate guarantee.

items.i1: 🔌 LIA speaks both generations of the MCP protocol — the Model Context Protocol published a major revision that older clients cannot talk to. LIA now speaks the new stateless revision AND automatically falls back to the classic handshake: every MCP server you already configured keeps working unchanged, and new-generation servers plug in too. If a server requires a revision LIA does not speak, you now get a clear explanation instead of a cryptic connection error.
items.i2: 🔐 Hardened OAuth for MCP servers — and declining is no longer an error — the OAuth flow applies the new specification's security obligations: the authorization server's identity is verified before your authorization code is used, and stored client credentials are never sent to a different authorization server than the one that issued them (LIA re-registers automatically instead). If you decline the consent screen at the provider, you come back to your settings with a simple informational message — not an error page.

v1_30_5.title: v1.30.5 — 🕐 Costs that follow the provider's clock

items.i1: 🕐 LLM costs now follow peak and off-peak hours — some providers (like DeepSeek) charge half price outside their peak UTC windows, and LIA used to count every call at the full rate. The pricing catalogue now supports time-based tariffs: each call is valued at the tariff of its exact moment, so your usage statistics and the instance spend ceiling reflect what the provider actually invoices. Admins define the windows in the LLM pricing settings — any provider, any number of windows.
items.i2: 📱 The pricing forms work on your phone again — the create/edit dialogs for LLM, Google API and image tariffs could be taller than the screen with their top out of reach, making them unusable on mobile. The scroll behaviour is fixed on all three: short forms stay centered, tall ones scroll from the very top.

v1_30_4.title: v1.30.4 — ✅ Confirmations that always tell the truth

items.i1: ✅ A refused action is never again announced as done — a real incident showed it: an oversized relayed message was refused internally, yet the answer said “Message delivered”. Fixed at the root: every tool's verdict (success or failure) now travels unchanged all the way to the answer. If something could not be done, LIA tells you, with the actual reason.
items.i2: 📏 An oversized relayed message is explained with its numbers — messages relayed to your connections are limited to 2,000 characters (instance-tunable). If yours exceeds it, LIA now gives you the exact length and the limit, and offers to shorten or summarize it — instead of a generic question that never named the real problem.
items.i3: 🔢 Bulk-operation confirmations show the exact count — the confirmation card states the number of items actually measured (never the theoretical cap), with correct singular wording when there is only one.

v1_30_3.title: v1.30.3 — 🧱 Foundations that no longer depend on someone else's weather

items.i1: 🔤 Fonts now ship with the application — building a new version no longer downloads fonts from Google: the exact files (same families, same weights, identical rendering) live in the repository. Two updates had failed the day before because Google moved its files at the wrong moment — that failure class is gone, and an automated guard forbids its return.
items.i2: 📦 Self-host installation is qualified end to end — for administrators: every candidate version is now actually installed, on two architectures (PC and Raspberry Pi), in a disposable hermetic environment, before any publication. Seven defects in the qualification process were fixed one by one, each proven on a real run. This version ships the repaired end-to-end chain: build → qualification → publication.

v1_30_2.title: v1.30.2 — ⚙️ An up-to-date agent engine and bounded spending

items.i1: ⚙️ The agent engine catches up on five months of fixes — the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem orchestrating every conversation moved to its latest versions, fully validated in an isolated environment first (8,489 tests executed before touching anything). In practice: fewer wasted calls, more reliable resumes after confirmations, and a deep fix to nested-agent persistence.
items.i2: 💸 Paid tools get a per-request ceiling — generating an image or querying Perplexity or Brave is now bounded per request: an agent looping on a billed API is stopped gracefully with an explanation instead of spending silently. Six tools covered, configurable, verified at startup.
items.i3: 🧠 History is no longer lost when its summary fails — when a long conversation is summarized to fit the model's memory, a failed summary used to mishandle the history; it is now fully preserved. And each model's memory window is read from the managed catalogue, not from a frozen table.
items.i4: 🔌 Closing the tab really stops the work in progress — an abandoned response stream now cancels the sub-agents it had launched, instead of letting them burn tokens on an answer nobody will read.

v1_30_1.title: v1.30.1 — 🧾 Exact accounting and failures that name themselves

items.i1: 📊 The “successful actions” counter finally works — it had shown 0 since forever: an internal classification defect counted every completed action as a plain answer, and “confirmed useful results” shrank to routines alone. Fixed and test-pinned — and your cycle's history has been reclassified, not just the future.
items.i2: 🧭 Repairable failures name themselves — rejected API key, exhausted provider credit, nonexistent model name: each case now has its precise message in all 6 languages, pointing at the exact screen where the repair lives. No more “service saturated, retry” on errors retrying will never fix.
items.i3: ⏱️ The timeout setting is actually applied — the admin “timeout” field existed from the screen down to the database, then nobody read it. It now reaches every provider, and the defaults were recalibrated against 30 days of real production latencies — without ever cutting a call that used to succeed.
items.i4: 🧾 Token accounting becomes a contract — every provider declares its accounting mode (verified at startup), the count is requested explicitly, and a paid call completing without usage triggers an alert: the spend ceiling can no longer go blind in silence.
items.i5: 🤖 A more resilient assistant on imperfect answers — truncated JSON, a trailing comma or prose around the payload are recovered instead of causing costly retries, and an empty answer is no longer memorized and replayed for five minutes.

v1_30_0.title: v1.30.0 — 📍 On the move, LIA answers from where you are

items.i1: 📍 Your real position, everywhere — when your phone's live position is unavailable (an app left dormant does this), LIA now uses your last remembered position — if you enabled it — before falling back to your home address. This applies to chat, scheduled actions, the briefing and skills alike: 'restaurants nearby' while travelling stops answering from your living room.
items.i2: 🕐 A dated position says so — 'where am I?' without a live GPS used to answer 'enable geolocation'. It now answers from your remembered position with its age stated: 'based on your last known position at 9:30' — never presented as your current spot. And 'at home' is never resolved from a position captured on the road.
items.i3: 🔔 The mobile app wakes up by itself — on return to the app, your position refreshes silently when the permission is still granted; when the system dropped it (iOS does this after inactivity), a banner offers to re-enable it right when you open the chat — before you have to ask. The 'remember my last position' setting now lives on the Google Places connector, next to the home address, with the stored position, its date and a delete button.
items.i4: 📞 Honest phone-call errors — when the telephony provider rejects your key (ElevenLabs now requires keys starting with sk_), LIA says exactly that and what to do, instead of a misleading 'try again in a moment'.
items.i5: 🛠️ Four production fixes — the autonomous ReAct mode no longer fails on Gemini when an MCP tool declares a list parameter; the LLM admin dialog no longer loops on a 422 error when switching models; skill widgets keep their Docker access after every deployment; and a fresh multi-worker start boots in about a minute instead of respawning for twenty.

v1_29_0.title: v1.29.0 — 🏠 LIA installs on your machine, and an instance knows what it spends

items.i1: 🏠 Install LIA on your own machine, guided — ./install.sh asks a short questionnaire in your language, builds the images from the source you cloned, creates your administrator account and your provider keys without ever writing a secret on the command line, and then checks that the installation really works — not merely that the server answers. If a step fails, ./install.sh --resume picks up exactly where it stopped.
items.i2: 💶 A daily spend ceiling for the whole instance — an administrator can now cap what the entire deployment spends in a day, in euros, and not only what each account consumes. First come, first served; afterwards LIA says come back tomorrow and gives the exact time it resets. The panel shows today's spend, the ceiling that really applies, and what is left.
items.i3: 🎛️ Switch a feature off in two seconds, without redeploying — dictation, speech synthesis, images, uploads, document spaces, web search, browsing, skills, MCP and telephony are now ten switches in the admin panel. Each row shows what the deployment allows, what the administrator chose, and what is actually applied — a capability the deployment forbids says so instead of pretending to be adjustable.
items.i4: 🎬 A guided demonstration, at /demo — six missions, one per mechanism that sets LIA apart: a crowded morning, a proactive alert, long-term memory, a phone booking, the daily briefing, and a tour of the settings. Approve, edit or refuse each prepared change, then read the final reply. Everything is labelled as a demonstration on synthetic data at every step, no external service is contacted, and a proof drawer links each element to its source.
items.i5: 📜 Terms of use accepted at sign-up — creating an account now requires an explicit acceptance, recorded with its date and version. The terms are written in the six languages, and this applies to every sign-up path.
items.i6: 🔒 Three faults the green test suite could not see — speech synthesis was billed but never counted against the spend ceiling; signing in with Google skipped the terms acceptance entirely; and eleven connector paths could link a real credential with no guard at all. All three are closed, and the new guards were deliberately broken to prove they go red.

v1_28_0.title: v1.28.0 — 🧭 LIA learns your habits, under your control

items.i1: 🧭 LIA can learn your habits — if you turn it on — your activity rhythm (your usual weekday and weekend slots) and your recurring requests ("every Monday morning, the emails") are learned through transparent statistics, never an opaque model. Everything is off by default, and everything lives in Settings → Learn my habits. Nothing leaves your account.
items.i2: 📊 A panel that shows everything — a heat map of your 24 hours with an hour axis, your active-day percentage, your detected windows — and when there is no stable habit, the panel says so honestly instead of inventing one.
items.i3: ⏳ You always know where learning stands — a progress bar shows observation days acquired versus required, and recurring requests under observation appear with their progress ("3/4 distinct days") before they are even confirmed.
items.i4: 🔍 "Why this habit?" — every habit explains itself: the real days it was observed and the exact thresholds the detector applies. A displayed habit is proven, or it does not exist.
items.i5: 🕰️ Notifications at the right moment, without nagging — LIA can notice a missed routine (at most once a day, and it goes permanently quiet after two ignored remarks) and prefer your usual slots for its notifications — never exceeding the hours YOU set.
items.i6: 🧹 Total, immediate control — pause a habit, block it forever (never relearned), delete everything, or relaunch learning over your history in one click: the "Recompute now" button acts immediately and retroactively.

v1_27_14.title: v1.27.14 — 🛡️ Updates that leave the app running

items.i1: 🛡️ An update no longer degrades the app while it installs — during a release, push notifications, the FAQ and the skills briefly stopped working: the update replaced the files underneath the running application. Updates now prepare everything aside and switch over in one move, so nothing is missing while the new version is being built.
items.i2: 💬 A conversation in progress is no longer cut off by an update — a chat being streamed was interrupted when a new version was installed. The application now finishes what it started before it stops.
items.i3: 💾 Database backups are actually kept — the scheduled dumps were stored inside the folder each update replaced, so they were erased every time. They now live outside its reach. If you administer an instance, check that your backup path points outside the deployment folder.
items.i4: 🌍 Messages from the assistant come back in your language — some replies and tool results fell back to their English source text whatever language you had chosen. The translation catalogues are now shipped with the application.
items.i5: ⏳ An account awaiting activation sees the page that explains the wait — a new sign-up whose account had not been activated yet landed on an application that looked broken, with every screen refusing to load. It now goes straight to the page describing the next step.
items.i6: 🔔 Push notifications stop chasing a device that no longer exists — when an app was uninstalled or its notification permit rotated, the assistant kept trying to reach it for days. Such a device is now retired on its first definitive refusal.

v1_27_13.title: v1.27.13 — 🔁 An action never replays itself

items.i1: 🔁 A clicked action no longer re-runs when you return to the chat — “Prepare a reply to the email…” could execute again when the browser resurrected the click's address (history, session restore). Every click now carries a one-shot id: a replayed address only prefills the composer, and you decide whether to send. “Run it now” links on proposed routines stay deliberately replayable — there, each click is a consent.
items.i2: 📥 Rich-HTML answers no longer crush their key-value lists — a long label (an email subject) squeezed the value column into an unreadable sliver overflowing the bubble. The layout is fixed, and answers already received display correctly again — nothing to do on your side.
items.i3: ⭕ The context gauge is visible on mobile — the pill showing how full the conversation is (with its totals tooltip on tap) joins the centre of the chat header, right of the knowledge-spaces indicator, at every screen size.
items.i4: 📊 The dashboard's Consumption opens expanded — messages, tokens, Google requests and cost are readable without an extra click; the section still folds if you prefer it quiet.
items.i5: 📤 Export is a visible button on phones — Long-term memory, Interests and Personal journals now show Export right in the toolbar instead of folding it into the “⋯” menu; the bar wraps cleanly on small screens.

v1_27_12.title: v1.27.12 — 🔬 The debug panel reads like the run

items.i1: 🧭 The trace follows the execution order — seven numbered phases (request, router analysis, planning, execution, response context, background extraction, totals) replace an accumulated ordering where the query appeared after the routing decision.
items.i2: 🌊 A waterfall on the run's own timeline — every model call is positioned by its real start, shared between the pipeline and its background tasks: what ran in parallel and what serialized is read at a glance.
items.i3: 🔍 The invisible stages now have a section — the plan validator's verdict (informative: a rejected plan still executes), the ReAct loop against its published iteration cap, approval gates, context compaction, image-generation and voice-synthesis spend.
items.i4: ⚠️ Anomalies surface on the request header — failed steps, panic planning, critical token zones and payload drift are counted on each history entry, next to a scannable strip (route, engine, duration, tokens, cost): compare requests without unfolding them.
items.i5: 🧹 Idle sections fold away — on a conversational turn, two thirds of the sections carry no data; they collapse behind one per-phase disclosure instead of stacking N/A rows.
items.i6: 🎨 Readable in both themes — statuses take the design-system tokens of the five themes, pipeline nodes wear bi-theme identity families, and a stage that simply did not run shows neutral instead of a red FAIL.

v1_27_11.title: v1.27.11 — 🧭 Settings that read like an index

items.i1: 🧲 The gap between a label and its field finally renders — a defect in the label primitive meant every spacing setting was computed but never drawn: all forms lived with ~3 px whatever the code said. Fixed at the root and calibrated on real screenshots — every form now breathes the same way.
items.i2: ☰ One grammar for row actions — visible icons from tablet up, delete carrying its red at rest, and on phones a single named “⋮” menu. No more buttons revealed by hover that a keyboard user landed on without seeing anything.
items.i3: 📤 Export is back on phones and tablets for long-term memory and interests — it was simply removed below a desktop width — and “+ Add” keeps its label at every size.
items.i4: 🗂️ LIA Connections read as five foldable, icon-carrying sections whose badges say what waits inside — pending requests included — and both share directions display as mirrors: yours editable, theirs read-only.
items.i5: 📔 Personal journals fold their whole configuration behind one entry, move their buttons below the categories, and long entries clamp to three lines with “Show more”.
items.i6: ⏰ A routine says “Weekdays at 08:00” instead of naming five days, shows its next run and folds the rest — its card drops from about eight always-visible lines to three.
items.i7: 🔐 Authenticator apps (TOTP) now enroll from a switch, like every other feature — turning it on opens the ceremony, and the thumb only moves once the server confirms.
items.i8: 🧭 Connector groups are named “Google / Apple / Microsoft / external services”, and a data export finally explains its state: size and expiry when ready, generation and expiry dates plus what to do when expired.
items.i9: 🎛️ Every title carries an icon in the theme colour — notification frequency, travel weather (now foldable), each dashboard card in the customisation list — and grey badges are reserved for the inactive: “Enabled” is green, “pending” is blue.
items.i10: 🔔 Push notifications follow your global opt-in automatically — the per-feature duplicate switch that could silently mute proactive notifications is gone.
items.i11: 🫧 What comes from LIA stands out — in the thread, a proactive notification carries a light red wash that tells it apart from an answer; a pinned memory is framed in the theme colour, its pin set right before the text. On phones the action bars get compact — “Add”, “Clear”, “Import”, “URL” — to fit on one line, and a connection card frames “what I share” and “what they share” separately.

v1_27_10.title: v1.27.10 — 🎨 Screens you can read at a glance

items.i1: 🔴 A “high” notification no longer looks like a “medium” one — both rendered on a pale ground in two very close hues: on a real account, 89 high and 113 medium notifications were indistinguishable. Urgency is now carried by density, not hue alone: high fills, medium tints, low stays neutral. The difference holds in greyscale too.
items.i2: 🔢 The Alerts counts show before you open anything — the number that decides which section to open could only be had by opening it. The five totals now arrive with the page; the lists still wait for the fold.
items.i3: 🔘 Action buttons look alike everywhere — the relationship-card actions and the Alerts shortcuts adopt the outlined style used throughout the app.
items.i4: 🧠 A memory shown on a relationship card is now clickable — it was dead text: correcting it meant finding Settings, then the right section, by hand.
items.i5: 👤 A peer connection carries the app's own initials avatar, with its name in bold — a list of connections was told apart by reading, not by looking.
items.i6: 🎯 Contact-card icons take one colour per family — reach, dates, ties. The card already answered three questions; colour makes that structure visible.
items.i7: 📨 “Sent” and “received” each have their own colour — on relayed messages, on a relationship card's messages, and on exchanged emails. Only a small arrow separated them.
items.i8: 📅 Shared meetings and exchanged emails finally have a count, like their five neighbours — and every count in the app now wears the same colour.
items.i9: 📞 A call's objective is told apart from its summary — and a long objective no longer spills out of its tag: a tag is sized for a word, not a sentence.
items.i10: 📱 On a phone, two dense blocks are no longer shown — “Why does LIA think this?” and the interest-weight explanation pushed what you came to read off the screen. They stay whole on a wide screen.

v1_27_9.title: v1.27.9 — 🔭 Why LIA thinks that, and what it can do

items.i1: 🔍 “Why does LIA think that?” under every memory and journal entry — a folded block shows the signals behind the conclusion, their date and their role, with a Correct button. What is kept is a reference, never a copy: your text stays where you wrote it. Delete the conversation and the reference empties while the dated row stays — the content never comes back. Settings → Memories, or Settings → Journals.
items.i2: 🔔 An “Alerts” destination for everything addressed to you — relayed peer messages, proactive notifications, interest notifications, pending reminders and scheduled routines, in one screen instead of five different settings panels. Each section arrives folded with its count already shown, and paginates by ten: you choose what to open without having to open it to find out. No list is fetched until something is unfolded. Your usual settings links keep working.
items.i3: 🌌 A star chart of your capabilities — each capability is a star: filled when active, outlined when waiting to be lit, its size saying what it holds. The figure joins only the live ones, so its shape is your configuration. No level, no percentage, no comparison with anyone. Home → Capabilities.
items.i4: 📈 An interest's weight explains itself — the originating signal, the last mention, the last notification and the calculation itself. Explaining uncertainty is more useful than turning it into a score. Settings → Interests, under each topic.
items.i5: 📞 No option raised on a call is accepted on your behalf — debrief follow-ups now prepare the message instead of sending it, and what the other party actually proposed (date, place, extra cost) is shown before the possible follow-ups.
items.i6: ✍️ Your card titles are no longer truncated — up to four action chips per row ate a third of the width. One trigger now opens the action menu, so every row of every card has the same text width. The full label appears on hover.
items.i7: 👍 Your feedback on an interest notification is finally recorded — the archived card and the recording route used two different identifiers. One vote also marked every other card in the conversation as judged: fixed in both directions.
items.i8: 🎨 Thirty-one places in the interface painted nothing, or painted black — health and personality chart tooltips, gradients, animations: a colour syntax inherited from an earlier version of the styling engine, invalid since the migration.
items.i9: 🧮 Your interest ranking and the displayed weight no longer disagree — two calculations each carried their own default value; there is now only one.
items.i10: 🔗 “LIA connection” is the last section of a relationship card on mobile — as on a wide screen, and only once in the page.

v1_27_8.title: v1.27.8 — 🧭 What LIA produced, and what may interrupt you

items.i1: 👍 Your thumbs-up on a proactive notification is finally recorded — the archived card carried a fabricated identifier the recording route could not resolve, so every vote failed silently. No feedback had ever been recorded. Already-archived cards no longer show the button at all, rather than offering a gesture with no effect.
items.i2: ⏰ A routine no longer runs twice on the night the clocks change — the scheduled time exists twice that night, and the routine fired again sixty minutes later. 54 double runs measured across the 2026 transitions of seven time zones. Now at most one run per local day — without ever dropping today’s run when you test a routine ahead of time.
items.i3: 🔇 Eleven switches: being connected to a service is no longer being interrupted by it — to stop mail-driven nudges you had to disconnect the connector, losing the tool you ask with. Settings → Proactivity → Notification topics. Everything is on by default, and a switch that cannot produce anything says so (leave-by advice needs the calendar).
items.i4: 📜 The settings finally show what they produced — the last ten proactive notifications and, identically, the interest ones: date, content, sources, verdict already given. Until now you could tune a frequency without ever seeing the result. Interest notifications older than this version show without their text: it was not kept, and a reconstructed summary would be worse than an absence.
items.i5: 📁 Three blocks fold, closed by default — the eleven switches and the two histories. The panel becomes an index you open rather than a wall you scroll past, and a closed block costs no request. The number of refused topics stays on the header: folding must not hide a decision.
items.i6: ✨ The empty chat offers what LIA already knows about your day — a meeting to prepare, a batch of mail, a commitment waiting, a pending reminder. Nothing is fetched to produce them: no connector woken, no quota spent. With nothing to go on, the generic starters come back.
items.i7: 🏆 The dashboard opens on your results, not your consumption — results confirmed useful, successful actions, routines run, commitments closed. Messages, tokens and costs move under “Consumption”. “Time saved” was dropped rather than estimated: nothing here measures it.
items.i8: 🤝 Share an answer with a connected peer — under an assistant bubble, the “…” menu lists your accepted peers and prepares the request in the composer. Nothing is sent without your confirmation.
items.i9: ✅ A commitment’s actions are where you read it — mark done, dismiss and correct, straight from the “For you” card on the dashboard. The full ledger stays one click away.
items.i10: 🎨 Also — LIA’s portrait is chosen from two visible thumbnails; a routine duplicates without creating anything before you confirm; the preview of the next five runs shows the time in the routine’s own zone and flags clock changes; a reminder cancels from its card; the photo gallery is fully keyboard-navigable; three quick commands join the list; and a brief haptic accompanies gestures on mobile, set separately from reduced animations.

v1_27_7.title: v1.27.7 — 🗣️ A real question rather than an error message

items.i1: 🗣️ When LIA is stuck it asks a question — not its own diagnosis — for_each pattern issue detected, Fabricated placeholder contact detail: step_2.to='jerome@example.com': that is what a French-speaking account received when LIA refused to run a doubtful plan. Jargon, a code path, and a made-up address you could believe came from your own address book. Now fifteen clear questions, in all six languages — and the app refuses to start if one is missing.
items.i2: ✉️ An address you gave is never reinvented — you specify a recipient and, two turns later, LIA writes to jerome@example.com. The value you gave is now carried over. A genuine change of mind on your side is never overwritten.
items.i3: ✍️ Correcting a commitment LIA misheard — the ledger fills itself from your conversations, so it is sometimes wrong: an approximate wording, a "by Friday" read as the wrong Friday. The text and the deadline can now be edited. The other party and the meaning cannot: changing them would describe a different commitment, not correct this one.
items.i4: 🤝 A commitment's actions, on the person's card — done, follow up, no longer relevant, correct: those gestures existed only in the settings. They are now on the matching relationship's card as well — where you actually think of them.
items.i5: 🏷️ "Open loops" is now called "Commitments" — and the section moves up to Settings → Features, next to Interests. The settings search knows both words: if you knew it under the old name, you still find it.
items.i6: 📇 A relationship card reads better — the contact card always opens the left column (knowing who this is comes before everything else) and the LIA connection always closes it. The details now read as three blocks: how to reach, which dates matter, who the person is tied to.
items.i7: 🔁 An instruction is no longer lost when you answer a question — you answered a request for clarification and, with nothing to show for it, the instruction your answer was meant to trigger vanished when the conversation resumed. It survives now.
items.i8: 🧭 What LIA claims it can produce is checked before every delivery — thirteen tool descriptions promised data they do not return: weather, web search, Wikipedia, reminders, routes, task lists. LIA built plans on those promises and failed halfway through. An automated check now compares every promise to the real result.
items.i9: ⚙️ For the administrator: the skill-creation guide described steps that do not exist — it announced two step types the engine rejects and kept silent about two it accepts, so a skill written by following the documentation was rejected at execution. Fixed in all six languages, and a check now blocks any divergence between the guide and the engine.

v1_27_6.title: v1.27.6 — 🔗 Every request leaves with the right name

items.i1: 🔗 A request no longer leaves carrying the previous name — a 360° overview of someone, then another person's card opened and launched, sent the first one's sentence. The browser alone decides the address now: what you launch is what you asked for, including when the link only prefills the input box.
items.i2: 📞 A question about a call gets an answer, not a call — "when did I last call Marie?" could produce a plan to phone her and ask. LIA can now read your past calls, your open commitments and your relayed messages, instead of only having the means to act.
items.i3: 🤝 Merge two cards that are the same person — LIA groups what is written the same, accents and capitals aside. It cannot guess that a raw phone number and a name are one relationship: you tell it, once, from the bottom of the card. It is reversible, and you always see what was merged.
items.i4: ✉️ An excerpt of the email under its subject — "Re: Re: catch-up" says nothing about what the exchange was about. Up to two lines now appear under the subject, on the relationship card.
items.i5: 📇 Calling a number no longer creates a second card — calling "06 12 34 56 78" then "Marie Martin" built two relationships for one person. The number is recognised and attached to the right card.
items.i6: 📱 Buttons you can actually hit with a finger — six controls were too small on a phone screen, including the cross that minimises the companion: invisible without a mouse, yet clickable. They now meet the recommended size.
items.i7: ⚙️ For the administrator: LIA can know what it already knows about a connected contact — when a connected person is named in the conversation, their commitments, calls and your relayed messages can be handed to LIA directly rather than announced as a lookup. Off by default, enabled by PEER_CONTEXT_INJECTION_ENABLED, and limited to what you ticked in the 360° scope.

v1_27_5.title: v1.27.5 — 👥 The 360° overview of a person, complete and configurable

items.i1: 👥 The 360° overview of a contact works again — asking for a 360° overview of someone answered that LIA could not retrieve their recent interactions. The tool did exist, but was never loaded at startup: LIA picked it, then could not find it. It now finds the mail exchanged and the meetings shared, searching by address rather than by name — far more reliable.
items.i2: 📇 The contact card shows your whole address book — nickname, job title, birthday, note, postal addresses, family relations, links, important dates and messaging handles join the name, organization, emails and phone numbers. What your provider does not store simply does not appear, rather than showing up empty.
items.i3: 🎯 You choose what the 360° overview reads — a new section at the top of a relationship card lets you tick the sources to use, tell received exchanges from sent ones and meetings the person attends from those they organize, and set how many items each section contributes. Your choice is saved before the chat opens: LIA applies it, it does not guess it.
items.i4: 🔢 LIA no longer under-counts what it summarizes — the card shows "137 commitments" and lists only a few; the assistant received those few rows alone and answered "you have five". It now receives the exact count. And when a source could not be read, it says so instead of announcing there was nothing.
items.i5: 👤 The 360° overview covers the person on screen, guaranteed — pressing the button used to send a sentence LIA had to re-interpret; it could pick generic tools and miss the point. The button now carries the request itself: the 360° tool is in the plan, on the right person. Other useful lookups are kept.
items.i6: 💬 The assistant finally receives everything the 360° found — it could answer "I have no data at hand" right after retrieving open commitments, calls and relayed messages. The content stopped on the way, before reaching it. It now arrives in full.
items.i7: 🤝 A LIA contact who is not in your address book finally has their mail and meetings — exchanges are found by address, and a connected person you never saved had none. If they turned on address sharing, LIA uses it to find, in your mail and your calendar, what concerns you both.
items.i8: 📅 No more event of YOUR calendar presented as theirs — with no shared meeting to show, the assistant filled the gap with the next entry in your own calendar, one the person neither organised nor attended. An empty section is an answer; a meeting without them is an error.

v1_27_4.title: v1.27.4 — 📧 Asking for 3 emails gives you 3 emails

items.i1: 📧 LIA no longer claims it failed when it succeeded — asking for "my last 3 emails" sometimes answered that the retrieval had been blocked and that you should go check your email connector. The emails had been fetched, the connector was healthy, and the whole diagnosis was wrong. The answer now reports a failure only when something genuinely produced nothing.
items.i2: 🧩 A partly blocked request shows what it did get — when one capability fails while another works, LIA presents the results it obtained and names what was missing, instead of announcing a total failure.
items.i3: ⚙️ Per-service result limits are honoured to the letter — the limit each connector sets on how many items can be read at once is now handed to the planner, which sizes its requests accordingly. Any value above it is brought back within range before execution rather than failing the plan.

v1_27_3.title: v1.27.3 — 🤝 Asking about a connected person now works

items.i1: 🤝 « Is Jérôme free tomorrow at 10? » — asking about someone you are connected to now answers from THEIR calendar, the one they chose as their default, at the hours you read on your own clock. All-day entries (a birthday, a reminder) are told apart from real meetings, so a birthday no longer makes someone look busy all day.
items.i2: 🎯 LIA no longer guesses when it is blocked — when a request cannot run, the answer names exactly which capability was missing and stops there. No more sweeping « nothing is configured » about services that work perfectly well, and no more blaming you for a fault that may be on our side.
items.i3: 🔌 A disconnected service now stays visible — instead of a single alert you may have missed, a discreet banner remains for as long as the connection is broken, with a Reconnect button. It disappears by itself the moment the service works again.
items.i4: ✏️ Your /shortcuts are editable — you can now change the name or the text of a shortcut you already created, instead of deleting it and starting over.
items.i5: ✨ A few comfort touches — the chat composer takes the same frosted-glass look as the header, the settings search moves above the tabs, card titles line up with their icon, and the « How LIA works » introduction is one sentence again.
items.i6: 📧 « Summarise this email and draft a reply » now completes every time — this request used to fail, then go through minutes later with nothing changed. LIA could end up having to reply to a message without any way to read it. It now checks it has everything it needs before starting, instead of finding out midway.

v1_27_2.title: v1.27.2 — 🌌 The public site gets its identity

items.i1: 🌌 A new visual identity — the home page and every public page (More, demo, Story, Philosophy, Technical, FAQ, blog) move to the cosmic theme: starfield background, a planetarium of features orbiting the live demo, and animations that play at the pace of your scroll.
items.i2: 🌓 Dark by default — public pages open in dark when you have never picked a theme; your theme button always wins, and your choice is remembered.
items.i3: ✅ Better readability — buttons, badges and pills all move back above the recommended contrast threshold, in light and dark alike.
items.i4: 🗓️ A more useful “For you” card — it now shows only the next upcoming automation, no more history. And a thumbs-up or thumbs-down on a proactive notification no longer pops an error message.
items.i5: 📱 Settings on narrow screens — the “My connectors” rows no longer overflow, the “Add a passkey” button moves below its text, “Recent calls” sticks to the last ten, and the skill-import buttons sit under their own separator.

v1_27_1.title: v1.27.1 — ⭐ Your relations, front and center

items.i1: ⭐ Relations in the navigation — the personal-CRM page gets its own entry in the bar (Knowledge stays one click away in the chat — its pill now always shows). Redesigned cards: initials avatars, colored signal pills, and a 360° sheet.
items.i2: ❤️ Persisted favorites — star anyone in one tap, without opening their card: your favorites keep their own band at the top, survive quiet periods, and a name filter appears once the list grows.
items.i3: 🤝 The LIA badge — relations who are also connected users of your instance carry a small badge, bridging your CRM and your connections.
items.i4: 🧭 Better findability — searching the settings for peers, social, discovery or loved ones now finds the Connections section; the « How LIA works » cards render their formatting properly.

v1_27_0.title: v1.27.0 — 🤝 Connect with people you know

items.i1: 🤝 Peer connections — two users of the same LIA instance can now connect: enable discovery in Settings, share your exact name, accept or decline requests in one click from the chat or the new Connections section. Nothing is shared by default.
items.i2: 💬 Assistant-to-assistant messages — ask LIA to tell something to a connection: you confirm before anything leaves, then the recipient's own assistant delivers it in its personality and language, naming you — and your assistant confirms delivery.
items.i3: 🗓 Chosen read-only shares — per connection, you can open your calendar availability (or details) and task titles, in both directions and visible to both sides; every access is recorded in a consultable log, and you can revoke at any time.
items.i4: ✨ Frosted-glass interface — dialogs, menus, toasts and the chat header now show a real glass effect (content slides beneath the blur), and native controls (dropdowns, scrollbars) finally follow dark mode.

v1_26_4.title: v1.26.4 — 📞 Your call reports, in your language

items.i1: 📞 Phone calls · Reliable report — the report LIA sends you after a call now always arrives in your language, with the structured debrief (key points, commitments, open questions). Some AI model configurations silently degraded it to a raw English technical summary; that whole failure class is now closed.
items.i2: 🛡️ Admin · Configuration guardrail — saving an AI model configuration whose reasoning mode would starve the response budget is now rejected with an explicit message stating the required token floor — instead of failing silently on the next call.

v1_26_1.title: v1.26.1 — 🎨 Answers with real page design

items.i1: 🧩 Rich HTML mode gains real components — colored callouts with titles, badges with icons, collapsible sections, key-value lists, side-by-side columns, numbered steps and key-figure tiles. LIA uses them sparingly, when they genuinely help reading. Display mode "Rich HTML", under Settings > Personalization.
items.i2: 🌈 Code comes out highlighted — in Rich HTML mode, code blocks now get syntax highlighting and a copy button, just like in the other modes.
items.i3: 📋 Copying an answer gives clean text — copying, sharing or exporting a Rich-HTML answer now produces readable, structured text (and a rich rendering where pasting supports it), never raw HTML code again.
items.i4: 🔍 Polish — history search no longer breaks icon rendering; phantom line breaks in HTML answers are gone; inline code is clearly visible again in light theme.

items.i1: 🎬 Act straight from your dashboard cards — every card now offers immediate actions: summarize a document, draft a reply to a mail, mark a task done, reschedule. The action runs through the chat as usual, with the same approval step for anything that writes to the outside world.
items.i2: ✂️ Select a passage of an answer — a small action bar appears (a bottom sheet on mobile): explain, rephrase, translate, turn it into a task or a reminder, save it to memory, or ask a question about it.
items.i3: ⏰ Routines that wait for the right moment — a routine can trigger on a condition (a task is overdue, a matching mail arrives, the weather turns, a document is added, an event approaches) instead of a fixed time, with a « propose first » mode that notifies you rather than acting on its own.
items.i4: 👥 A personal CRM — see in one place everything LIA already knows about a person: open commitments, recent calls, remembered facts. Reachable from the dashboard's Quick Access.
items.i5: 📞 A richer call debrief — after a call: outcome, commitments made, tasks and reminders created, open questions, and a one-tap follow-up draft.
items.i6: 🕐 The dashboard tells the truth about freshness — « updated X ago », served from cache, last attempt when something goes wrong, and a one-click retry per card.
items.i7: 📚 Knowledge made easier to reach, plus shortcuts — Knowledge Spaces join the menu, the chat indicator is centered and discreet; installed on your home screen, LIA offers shortcuts (today's priority, quick add, push-to-talk), and an admin can create their own « / » commands.

v1_25_33.title: v1.25.33 — 📋 Paste, share, drive the demo

items.i1: 📋 Paste a screenshot straight into the chat — Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on Mac) with an image or PDF in the clipboard: the file is attached exactly as through the paperclip, same limits, same preview. Paste text along with a file and both arrive.
items.i2: 📤 Share or export an answer — a "…" menu at the bottom of every answer: send it to your apps (Messages, Mail, Notes…) when your device offers a share sheet, or download it as a dated Markdown file, accents preserved.
items.i3: 🎙️ The send button finally says what it does — empty field: a microphone shows when "hold to speak" is available; some text: the send icon; voice unavailable: a clearly disabled button. No more button inviting you to speak when it can't.
items.i4: 🎯 A real drop zone — drag an image or PDF towards the conversation: a clear "Drop your images or PDFs here" zone appears instead of a thin ring around the field.
items.i5: 🧩 "Customize" next to "Refresh all" — pick your dashboard cards and their order without digging through the settings: the button leads straight to the right section.
items.i6: 🎬 The demo is now yours to drive — on the public home page and /demo: pick the scene (She orchestrates, She anticipates, She calls, She extends herself), pause, replay. Without interaction, the loop keeps cycling as before.
items.i7: ✨ A small celebration — completing the starter checklist makes its check sparkle — once, and never if your system asks for reduced motion.

v1_25_32.title: v1.25.32 — 🔍 Find a setting by its name

items.i1: 🔍 A search field in settings — the page stacks some thirty collapsed sections across several tabs. Type the name of a setting: the search takes you straight there, switches tab if needed, opens the right section and places the cursor on it.
items.i2: 🗂️ Thirteen more settings become findable — Language, Appearance, Timezone, Font, Display mode, Strong authentication, My devices, Export my data, Image generation and a few others could only be reached by scrolling. They now have their own address and show up in the search.
items.i3: 🌍 The search understands your words, in all six languages — every setting carries a translated list of synonyms: "dark" finds Appearance, "2FA" and "TOTP" find Strong authentication, "GDPR" finds the data export, "cron" finds Scheduled actions.
items.i4: ✍️ Accents and apostrophes no longer block a search — typing "theme" finds "Thème", and "d'authentification" finally reaches the section whose text carried a typographic apostrophe. The fix also benefits the search in this FAQ.
items.i5: ⌨️ Everything works from the keyboard — arrows walk the results, Enter opens, Escape dismisses then clears. The number of matches is announced to screen readers, and the cursor lands on the section you picked.
items.i6: 💬 A missing setting says so — some sections only appear when the feature is active on your account. Rather than leaving you in front of a page that did not move, LIA tells you the section is not showing here.
items.i7: 📊 The figures on the "Directing an AI that codes" page were out of date — it claimed half the real number of tests and a third of the documented architecture decisions. They have been measured again.

v1_25_31.title: v1.25.31 — 📌 Headers finally stay in place

items.i1: 📌 The top bar no longer scrolls away — the header of the dashboard and of the legal pages was meant to stay pinned while you scroll. It never did: it drifted off with the page, on every screen, since the very beginning. It now stays where it belongs, so navigation is one click away wherever you are on a page.
items.i2: 🧭 Settings tabs stay with you — the settings page stacks about thirty sections. Once a few screens down, nothing told you which tab you were in, and switching meant scrolling all the way back up. The tabs now follow you down the page.
items.i3: 🍔 The logo menu no longer makes the header vanish — on a phone, opening the menu from the middle of a page pushed the top bar off-screen, and you had to scroll back to the very top before it would work again.
items.i4: 📱 Denser settings on a phone — sections give back some padding on small screens only, so you scroll noticeably less. Nothing is hidden or shortened: every description stays whole, and the desktop layout is untouched.
items.i5: ⚡ Help and Settings in one compact bar — the two large cards above your briefing became a single bar, freeing roughly 85 px on a phone for the content that matters. Both destinations keep their label and their description, and they are real links now: middle-click or open them in a new tab.
items.i6: 👍 Feedback in the same place on every message — the thumbs of proactive notifications and of interest notifications sat inside the bubble, under a full sentence. They now sit next to the copy button, exactly like on an ordinary answer. Once you have voted, your choice stays visible instead of disappearing — shown as chosen, and locked, because that verdict is final.
items.i7: ♿ Settings read correctly to a screen reader — each section announced its title twice, and the group headings were not headings at all. The page structure is now what it looks like, which makes it navigable by headings.
items.i8: 📖 A section of the technical guide is reachable again — the “Psyche Engine” chapter was missing from the guide's table of contents, in all six languages, since the day it was written.

v1_25_30.title: v1.25.30 — 🛡️ An email can no longer give LIA orders

items.i1: 🛡️ Content written by other people is now labelled as such — an email body, an invitation description authored by its organiser, a web page, a place listing: LIA reads these every day, and anyone can slip instructions meant for it inside them. Every piece of data now carries its provenance, so the assistant knows it is material to analyse, never an order to follow. An unknown data type is treated as external by default.
items.i2: 🔎 Manipulation attempts are spotted and named — seven families of trap are detected across the app's six languages: fake system message, "ignore previous instructions", identity switch, requests to send your data elsewhere, invisible characters, hidden HTML comment. Your content is never rewritten: an email stays exactly what its author wrote, with a short note beside it.
items.i3: ⏱️ The time you take to approve no longer counts against the assistant — in autonomous mode the agent's clock kept running while the approval request waited for you. Past two minutes of thinking, the work in progress was cut and the answer rebuilt from scratch, losing the steps already completed. The budget now measures actual compute time only.
items.i4: 🔁 The autonomous assistant no longer goes in circles — nothing stopped it from calling the same tool with exactly the same arguments forever. On the fourth identical call it is asked to change approach; on the fifth the turn ends cleanly instead of burning your budget in a loop.
items.i5: 💸 Autonomous mode costs less and works with more models — its internal instructions were re-sent in full every turn, then at every step of every turn. They now go out once, which lightens the bill and unblocks providers that refused the conversation from the second exchange on.
items.i6: 🧹 A setting advertised a feature that no longer existed — the technical panel showed a "hybrid search" switch for memory, while that engine had been gone for several versions. The display and the dead code are removed. Hybrid search is still very real, but where it actually lives: in your knowledge spaces, over your documents. Your memories are retrieved by a dual semantic search instead — over their content and over their keywords.
items.i7: ⚙️ Admins: the memory alert no longer cries wolf — it counted the disk cache, which the system reclaims on its own, so it fired permanently on a perfectly healthy service. It now measures the quantity that actually decides a forced shutdown, the metrics service limit was raised, and a diagnostic runbook comes with it. An alert that fires finally means something.

v1_25_29.title: v1.25.29 — 🎯 Blocking a subject now means it never comes back

items.i1: 🚫 Blocking an interest finally sticks — you blocked a subject, and LIA re-created it twenty-five minutes later under a barely different name. Blocking was the strongest signal you had, and it was quietly undone. A blocked subject is now invisible to the whole learning loop: it can be neither re-created, nor renamed back into place, nor deleted out of the way.
items.i2: 🎯 Far fewer interests you never asked for — a subject you merely asked about became a lasting interest, so the proactive engine came back to you about things you had simply looked up once. Measured on real conversations: half of the exchanges that should have produced nothing were creating an interest; now none of them do, and the genuine ones are still caught.
items.i3: 🛡️ Your interest profile is protected from a runaway answer — one ordinary sentence was enough for LIA to propose deleting nineteen interests, that is your entire list. Deletions carried no confidence check of any kind. A single exchange can now remove at most a couple of subjects; beyond that the batch is refused and recorded.
items.i4: 👍 Proactive check-in notifications finally accept your feedback — the cards LIA sends on its own initiative had no thumbs at all, only the interest cards did. You can now tell it whether a check-in was useful, and it adjusts.
items.i5: 🗂️ Your verdicts now appear in the notification history — the feedback you gave was applied to the subject but left no trace in the history of what LIA sent you. Each verdict is now attached to the exact notification it came from.
items.i6: ⚙️ Administrators: the reasoning effort you pick is no longer erased — choosing an effort that happened to match the default silently stored nothing, and the three background analyses ran with no reasoning at all. Your choice is now kept whenever it fits the selected model.

v1_25_28.title: v1.25.28 — 🧠 What never made it into memory

items.i1: ✏️ Edit a skill by talking to LIA — until now LIA could create a skill but never adjust one. You can now ask it to tweak, enrich or fix one of yours: it re-reads the existing skill, applies your request, then shows you exactly what will be replaced and what will disappear before asking for your approval. Nothing is written until you confirm, and the skill's thumbnail is preserved.
items.i2: 💬 Your journals and LIA's mood now work from Telegram too — a conversation held on an external messenger fed neither your logbooks nor LIA's emotional state, even with both switched on. The setting was saved correctly, it simply was not passed along. A conversation is a conversation now, wherever you write from.
items.i3: 🧠 A request that triggers an action feeds memory again — when you asked, say, to send a message and slipped a fact about yourself into it, confirming the action lost that fact: neither memory, nor interests, nor the journal kept any trace of it. Those exchanges count again.
items.i4: 🔎 A contact with a common first name gets their memories back — LIA deliberately ignores contentless messages like ok or thanks. That filter also applied to people's names, and some of those words are real surnames: asking about a contact so named returned no memories at all, without any error message.
items.i5: 🌍 Fewer pointless computations across the six languages — a plain ja, gracias, grazie or 好的 triggered a full analysis while an ok or a thanks was correctly ignored. All six application languages are now treated equally.
items.i6: 🎯 More accurate interests — a subject you merely asked LIA to explain or look up could become an interest, though it committed you to nothing. LIA now records an interest only if you showed a lasting link to the subject — you love it, you practise it, you already know it, or you came back to it several times in the exchange — and it quotes your own words to justify it. Long-term memory follows the same demand: what you ask about is not what you are.

v1_25_27.title: v1.25.27 — 🔁 Coming back whole after an update

items.i1: 🔁 LIA comes back at full capacity after an update — right after an update the server rebuilds part of its internal index, and it was doing that work four times over at once. The provider refused, and two of the four processes serving you failed to start: for about a minute LIA answered on half its capacity, which showed up as slowness under load. That work is now done once, by one process, while the others simply wait for its result.

v1_25_26.title: v1.25.26 — 🧠 What LIA knows about itself

items.i1: 🧠 Answers about LIA are complete again — the built-in help LIA reads from had ended up holding three copies of every answer, so out of the five passages it consults, only two were actually different. It now holds exactly one copy of each, and if that ever drifts again the next restart repairs it on its own.
items.i2: 📚 Help updates reach you — refreshing the built-in help could fail silently at startup, leaving the version LIA quotes behind the product. Those failures are now visible and retried, and while one is being fixed the previous help keeps serving instead of disappearing.
items.i3: 🔄 The admin reindex button tells the truth — it announced a rebuild even when the help was already current, and even when another rebuild was already running. It now says which of the three actually happened.

items.i1: 🎨 High-quality images now make it through — a detailed image takes the provider over two minutes, but generation was cut off before that. You got nothing, with no explanation, and no setting could extend it. The time allowed for images is now based on their measured duration: high quality reaches the end.
items.i2: 🐈 Asking for an image stays a request for an image — "create a realistic image of a cat" sometimes went off to build a skill instead of drawing. The generation tool, correctly identified as the right one, was no longer even offered. The two now coexist: the requested action runs, and the detected skill adds to it rather than taking its place.
items.i3: 🧩 Importing a skill works again — every import failed, from the chat and from settings alike, because a storage folder had become unwritable for the application. The only visible sign was an error message in the middle of a reply.
items.i4: 🖼️ Skills finally show a preview — each skill's detail panel displayed an empty frame. All fourteen bundled skills now have their thumbnail: a sketch of what they produce — a calendar grid, a QR code, weather cards.
items.i5: 📱 No more replies stuck on your phone — when the phone suspends the tab, the connection dies silently: the screen stayed on "Generating the response…" forever, even though the answer was finished and saved. LIA now detects that silence and reconnects to the running answer on its own.

v1_25_24.title: v1.25.24 — 🧭 Finding what LIA already knows how to do

items.i1: 📱 The logo becomes your menu on a phone — below a certain width the navigation bar disappeared and nothing replaced it: from the chat you could reach neither settings nor help without typing a URL. Tap the LIA logo now and the four destinations open, with the current page announced.
items.i2: 🎯 Links land you on the right section — the getting-started checklist sent six of its seven items to the top of the settings page, in front of about thirty collapsed blocks. Each item now opens its own section, unfolds it and scrolls to it. Seventeen sections are addressable this way, including from the home cards.
items.i3: 🏠 Unconfigured home cards are no longer holes — seven of the nine cards render nothing at all until their source is connected, so a fresh account met two empty cards and seven unexplained absences. One discreet line now names them and links to the setting that switches each on. Cards you hid yourself are never mentioned.
items.i4: ⚠️ A warning before the usage wall — until now nothing signalled that your quota was close: the interface simply blocked, mid-task. A banner now appears at 80 % of whichever limit binds first, names it, and gives the reset date when it is a per-period limit.
items.i5: 🖼️ Generated images announce their deletion date — they are kept for a limited time and then removed. Nothing said so: the image vanished from the history without warning. Each card now states how long it stays available, and switches to an alert tone in its final hours.
items.i6: 🔁 A failed turn replays in one click — when a turn failed you had to find your question and retype it. A Retry button replays exactly the request that failed, even if other messages arrived in between.
items.i7: 💬 The FAQ examples are clickable — the hundreds of ready-made phrases in this FAQ had to be copied by hand. One click now drops them into the chat composer, ready to edit before sending. Nothing is ever sent on your behalf.
items.i8: 📞 Calls: followed during, explained after — between your confirmation and the recap, LIA went completely silent. A banner now says who she is calling and where the call stands, and a settings section keeps the history. Above all: a call refused by the carrier (unverified source number, exhausted credit) used to block every further call for a quarter of an hour — the refusal is now detected and explained instead of being mistaken for a call in progress.
items.i9: 🗣️ LIA no longer asks for the same confirmation twice — for an email, an appointment or a call she warned that the action was irreversible and waited for your agreement… while a preview and an explicit confirmation were coming right after. You had to insist to be obeyed. That duplicate question is gone; the confirmation that matters, the one showing exactly what will be sent, is of course still there.
items.i10: ✅ In-app confirmations, and an interface that fits the screen — the most final admin actions went through the operating system's own dialog, which ignores the theme and labels its buttons in the computer's language. They now use LIA's dialogs. Along the way: on mobile the composer no longer hides under the browser's address bar, and on a tablet the logout button no longer sits off-screen in German.

v1_25_23.title: v1.25.23 — 🔍 The tests that never ran

items.i1: 🔊 The voice no longer splits numbers in two — when LIA read out "it's 3.5 degrees", it said "it's three." and then, in a separate audio clip, "point five degrees". The dot of a decimal was taken for a full stop. Same for prices, version numbers and web addresses. A dot now ends a sentence only when a space follows it.
items.i2: ⏰ A reminder is no longer lost when your quota runs out at the wrong moment — if you had used up your usage budget in the exact minute a reminder was due, it was not postponed: it disappeared for good, with no error and no notification. It is now put back in the queue and reaches you on the next pass.
items.i3: 🌍 Notifications and follow-up questions in your language — reminder titles arrived in English for Chinese accounts, and whenever LIA asked you to clarify a change, the sentence was always in French whatever your language. All six languages are now served everywhere, including the wind direction on the weather card.
items.i4: ✏️ The value you correct stays in the conversation — when you answered "make it Jean instead" to a confirmation request, your correction replaced your original message with "run this tool with the modified parameters": the name you had just given vanished from the history. It is now preserved for every tool.
items.i5: ⚠️ Error messages finally tell you what happened — the detail returned by the server ("this model already exists", "invalid address") was replaced by a generic sentence, and a validation error displayed as "[object Object]". The real message now comes through everywhere. A server failure with an empty body is no longer mistaken for a silent success either.
items.i6: 🗑️ Confirmations name what they act on — a confirmation before deleting a label did not say which label, and deleting an email was presented to LIA as sending one, which switched off its caution rule for deletions. Every action is now announced for what it is.
items.i7: 🔧 On the admin side — the cost of each model call re-read the exchange rate from the database on every computation; it is now genuinely cached. The personality panel survives an expired session instead of freezing, and usage tracking shows the exact reason for a refusal rather than a generic message.

v1_25_22.title: v1.25.22 — 🔒 A sign-out that leaves nothing behind

items.i1: 🔔 Signing out really does stop notifications on that device — the push registration outlived the sign-out. On a shared computer or phone, the next person saw your notifications arrive on the lock screen without ever having signed in to your account. Signing out now revokes that device before closing the session.
items.i2: 📍 Your location no longer follows the next account — the last known position and the geolocation permission stayed in the browser after a sign-out. On a shared profile, the next account inherited your position for weather and places, and above all inherited your consent: the browser kept collecting the location of someone who had never agreed to it. Both are now cleared.
items.i3: 🔒 Nobody else can switch off your notifications — revoking a device did not check who owned it, so any other signed-in account could silently disable notifications on a device that was not theirs. Ownership is now verified.
items.i4: 💬 Telegram no longer answers the same message twice — when Telegram redelivered a message it had not seen acknowledged, LIA processed it a second time: the assistant answered twice, and a linking code was consumed twice. Each message is now handled exactly once.
items.i5: 🖼️ Images in a conversation no longer give the conversation away — displaying an image hosted elsewhere (a photo in an email, a fetched web page) told that image's server the address of your LIA page, conversation id included. It no longer does.
items.i6: 🛡️ On the admin side: two protections that were not protecting — an alert now genuinely fires when the API is running with no request ceiling (it existed, but in a file the monitoring never read), and a deployment stops if the server's secrets are not properly locked down, instead of reporting success without having checked anything.

v1_25_21.title: v1.25.21 — 📚 Document search stays on during upgrades

items.i1: 📚 Your documents stay searchable during an upgrade — when an administrator switches the model that indexes your document spaces, search used to go dark until the entire rebuild finished. The old index now keeps answering every query until the new one is fully ready, then switches over instantly, space by space — and resumes on its own if the rebuild is interrupted.
items.i2: 🛠️ One kind of upgrade still needs a short window — changing the size of the index (a rarer, deeper change) stays a planned maintenance moment, now clearly documented for administrators instead of silently returning nothing.

v1_25_20.title: v1.25.20 — 🔒 What runs, runs in a sealed box

items.i1: 📦 Skill scripts run in a sealed box — a skill's code now runs in a container created for that single run and destroyed right after: no network, no access to your files, no keys. You install a skill for what it produces, not for the trust you would have to extend to its author.
items.i2: 🖥️ Every server task asks for your approval — an administration request on a remote server is now prepared and submitted, never launched directly. That includes continuing an investigation already under way.
items.i3: 👁️ The confirmation shows everything that will be sent — the card displays the target server, the full task text and the instructions LIA wrote for itself. A summary you cannot read in full is not a confirmation.
items.i4: 📍 Your coordinates and tokens leave the logs — GPS positions join the masked parameters, and visited addresses finally pass through the privacy filter, including the ones that used to bypass it.
items.i5: 🧹 Switching accounts cleans the device — sensitive data kept locally is wiped on sign-out, and also when a different account signs in after a session has expired.
items.i6: 🗺️ Your maps belong to you alone — rendering maps and routes now requires your session and carries its own quota.
items.i7: 💬 The Telegram channel requires a secret — with no secret configured the webhook refuses every message instead of accepting them, and a leftover example value stops the application from starting.
items.i8: 🚦 The service stays available under a burst — a global ceiling now protects every route, sized far above real usage so it stays invisible in normal use.
items.i9: ⬆️ Oversized uploads are refused immediately — a file beyond the limit is rejected before being loaded, instead of occupying server memory only to end in an error.

v1_25_19.title: v1.25.19 — 🛡️ LIA asks before it acts

items.i1: 🛡️ A bulk action always asks first — “reply to each of these emails” could send up to nine replies without ever asking you. Replies, forwards, label changes and reminder cancellations are now all confirmed from the very first item.
items.i2: ✋ LIA no longer acts on its own — after an exchange, LIA may complete its answer by checking adjacent domains. Seven tools that MODIFY things (labels, completed tasks, lights, scripts) were wrongly eligible for that: they are excluded now.
items.i3: 🗑️ The bin stays in the bin — searching for “deleted invoices” silently pulled trashed messages back into the results, presented as ordinary mail. Only an explicit request for the bin includes it now.
items.i4: 📅 “Reschedule my meeting” moves it instead of duplicating it — the word “reschedule” was read as a creation, so LIA created a second event rather than moving yours.
items.i5: 📨 “Reply to each of these emails” runs again — on some results the list to iterate over was seen as empty and the action ran on nothing, with no error message.
items.i6: 💶 Fairer conversation costs — cached tokens were counted twice on one path, inflating the displayed cost. Billing now reflects real usage.
items.i7: 🔒 Hardened display cards — a link or a colour supplied by an external service could inject code into a card. Everything is filtered at the source now.
items.i8: 🔗 More reliable Apple and Microsoft connectors — a network error could make a failed update look successful, or lose contact data without warning.
items.i9: 🔑 Password policy locked down — the rule is applied identically by the browser and by the server, and that consistency is now checked automatically.

v1_25_18.title: v1.25.18 — 🎯 LIA says only what it checked

items.i1: 🎯 No more approximate details — when an exchange calls no tool, LIA now anchors on the data actually retrieved moments earlier instead of rephrasing from memory. It announced an appointment at “4pm” when the calendar had returned 11:15am: fixed.
items.i2: 🙋 A plain “I don’t know” instead of a guess — if a piece of information was never retrieved, LIA says so plainly rather than filling the gap with a plausible value.
items.i3: 🕐 Weather in your local time — three-hour forecast slots were shown in UTC; they now follow your own timezone.
items.i4: 🌍 Weather in your language — weather summaries were written in French whatever your language. They are now translated across the 6 languages.
items.i5: 📅 Out-of-range forecast: a clear answer — asking for weather too far ahead used to return a silent approximation. LIA now tells you how far the forecast actually reaches.
items.i6: 📍 Two appointments, two forecasts — when several items were enriched on the same day at the same place, one of them silently lost its data. Each now keeps its own.
items.i7: 🗺️ No more weather for a town that does not exist — a parameter left empty became the word “null”, and LIA looked for a place by that name. It now falls back to your own location.
items.i8: ❤️ Your health signals stop vanishing — nearly one proactive notification in two was prepared without your activity data. The read is 50× lighter, and any drop is now traced.

v1_25_17.title: v1.25.17 — 🔐 Your account grows a spine

items.i1: 🔑 Passkeys — sign in with Face ID, your fingerprint or your device code. Phishing-resistant, nothing to remember (Settings > Security).
items.i2: 📱 Authenticator app (TOTP) — add a 6-digit second step to password sign-in, with 10 single-use backup codes shown exactly once.
items.i3: 🛡️ Identity confirmation — sensitive actions (managing passkeys, exporting your data, signing out other devices) ask you to re-confirm who you are. Right after signing in, nothing to confirm for 5 minutes.
items.i4: 💻 My devices — see every session connected to your account (browser, system, approximate IP) and sign out one device or all the others.
items.i5: 🔔 New sign-in alerts — a push notification warns your devices when your account signs in from an unrecognized device. Can be turned off in My devices.
items.i6: 📦 Export my data — request a complete archive of your data (readable Markdown + JSON + your files); a notification tells you when it is ready to download.
items.i7: 📴 Offline mode — LIA now shows a proper offline page and loads faster thanks to smart caching. Your data is never cached on disk.
items.i8: 🎨 Reorganized Security settings — Strong authentication, My devices and Export my data are now three clean collapsible sections.

items.i1: 💬 Smarter input box — your draft survives a refresh or navigation, and ↑/↓ walk through your last 10 sent messages to re-edit them (like a terminal).
items.i2: 📌 Protected reading — while you scroll up to re-read, a streaming answer no longer drags you to the bottom. A floating button with a counter brings you back when YOU decide.
items.i3: 🔁 Follow-up suggestions — up to 3 tappable chips under the latest answer propose your likely next request; tapping fills the input, never sends.
items.i4: ⚡ Slash commands — type « / » in the chat: resume, briefing, agenda, search, plus everyday shortcuts (unread emails, weather, weekend weather, tasks, reminders, news) and your dialogue skills.
items.i5: 🧩 Your dashboard, your rules — hide or reorder the 9 briefing cards in Settings (a hidden card is not even fetched anymore); a starter checklist reveals what your instance can do; open commitments get their own consult/close section.
