q5.question: How does the approval system work?
q5.answer:
To protect your data, LIA uses an intelligent approval system (Human-in-the-Loop). Before any action that modifies your data, LIA asks for confirmation:

🔒 Actions requiring approval:
• Send, reply to or forward an email
• Create, modify or delete an event
• Create, modify or delete a contact
• Create or complete a task

📋 How it works:
1. LIA prepares a draft of the action
2. You see a detailed preview of what will be done
3. You can:
• ✅ Approve: the action is executed
• ✏️ Edit: correct before validation
• ❌ Cancel: nothing is done

💡 Tip: Take time to review the preview, especially for emails!

q6.question: Can LIA make mistakes?
q6.answer:
Like any AI assistant, LIA may sometimes misinterpret a request. Here's how to get the best results:

✅ Best practices:
• Be specific: "Send an email to john.smith@email.com" rather than "Send an email to John"
• Give context: "Find my emails from this week about the Alpha project"
• Review previews before approving actions

⚠️ If there's an error:
• Rephrase your request with more details
• Use specific dates ("January 15") rather than relative ones ("last week")
• For important emails, always review the preview

🛡️ Built-in security:
Thanks to the approval system, no critical action is executed without your explicit validation.

q7.question: How was LIA built?
q7.answer:
Nearly 100% of LIA's code is written by an AI, under human direction: written engineering rules, blocking automated checks, a review cycle where the human decides, and recurring adversarial audits (latest assessment: 8.3/10 across 24 areas — full report).

The full story — method, trade-offs, operations and what remains to be done — is on the Story page, and the source code is open on GitHub.

q8.question: Can I install LIA on my phone — as a PWA or a real app? (v1.33.0)
q8.answer: Yes, two ways. As a PWA: open your LIA in the browser and use “Add to Home Screen” — it launches full-screen, works offline, and on iOS 16.4+ even receives web push. As a native app (new): install the LIA app from the store, type your server's address once at the first screen, and you get the same interface plus what only a native app can do — sign-in through the system browser, native notifications (on Android straight from your server's own Firebase project; on iOS through a privacy-preserving wake relay), and connectors that return to the app after authorization. Your server stays the only place your data lives: the app is just a window onto it.

q9.question: My account says it is awaiting activation — what should I do?
q9.answer:
Signing up creates your account, but an administrator has to activate it before you can use LIA. Until then you land on a page that explains where you stand, and the rest of the application stays closed.

• You will receive an email as soon as your account is activated. Check your spam folder if you do not see it after a while — it is the most common reason people think nothing happened.

• Nothing is lost in the meantime. Your account already exists; activation only opens the door.

• If several days pass with no email, contact the administrator of your organisation, who can activate the account directly.

Before v1.27.14 this wait was invisible: the application loaded and then refused every screen, which looked like a breakdown rather than a pending step.

q10.question: Is there a mobile app for Android or iPhone?
q10.answer: Yes — one official app per store, and it works with any self-hosted LIA server. At first launch you type your server's address (HTTPS required); the app then loads your server's own interface, so every web improvement reaches it instantly with no store update. Google sign-in, notifications, and returning from a connected service (Gmail, calendar, MCP…) all work natively. If your server is unreachable, a built-in offline screen offers a retry and a way to switch servers. The web app and the PWA keep working exactly as before — the apps are an addition, never a replacement.

q1.question: Can I have multiple conversations at the same time?
q1.answer:
LIA works with one active conversation. This design choice buys you:

• A coherent context: LIA remembers the whole exchange
• Natural references: "the first email", "the previous contact"
• A smooth experience: nothing to juggle between windows

To start fresh:
Click the 🗑️ button in the chat header. It deletes every message and every attachment — AI-generated images included — so export anything you want to keep first.

q2.question: How do I reset a conversation?
q2.answer:
To clear everything and start over:

1. In the chat header, find the 🗑️ button
2. Click it
3. Confirm in the dialog

⚠️ What is actually deleted:
Every message, all your attachments — AI-generated images included, and the context LIA had built from this conversation. The action is irreversible.

💡 When is it worth it?
• You switch to a completely different topic
• LIA seems confused by earlier context
• You would rather not leave that history behind

q3.question: Are conversations saved?
q3.answer:
Yes, your conversation is saved as it happens:

• Real-time: every message is recorded the moment it is sent
• Multi-device: pick it up from any device signed in to your account
• Persistent: it survives logging out and closing the browser

📱 In practice:
Start a conversation on your computer and continue it on your phone — and back again.

🗑️ Deleting it is a deliberate act:
Nothing is removed until you use the 🗑️ button and confirm.

q4.question: How do I use line breaks in my messages?
q4.answer:
Two keyboard shortcuts to know:

• Enter = send the message
• Shift + Enter = new line

💡 Worked example:
To dictate a structured email, type:

Send an email to John:
Subject: Project meeting
Body:
Hello John,

I confirm our meeting tomorrow.

Best regards

Use Shift+Enter between each line, then Enter to send the whole thing at once.

q5.question: Does LIA remember the conversation context?
q5.answer:
Yes! LIA maintains an intelligent context throughout the conversation:

🔗 Contextual references:
• "Show my emails from John" → finds 3 emails
• "Reply to the second one" → LIA knows you're talking about the 2nd email
• "Add Sophie in CC" → LIA remembers the draft in progress

📋 What LIA remembers:
• Previous search results
• Contacts, emails, events mentioned
• Drafts awaiting approval
• The conversation thread

💡 Tip: Use natural references like "the first one", "Mary's one", "tomorrow's appointment".

q6.question: Why does LIA sometimes take time to respond?
q6.answer:
Response time varies based on your request's complexity:

⚡ Fast responses (1-3 seconds):
• Simple conversation questions
• Weather information
• Wikipedia searches

⏱️ Medium responses (3-10 seconds):
• Searching your emails
• Calendar consultation
• Contact search

🔄 Longer responses (10-30 seconds):
• Creating complex emails
• Combined multiple searches
• Actions requiring multiple steps

💡 Visual indicators:
During processing, you'll see messages like "🔍 Analyzing your request..." or "📋 Preparing action plan..."

The display itself is alive: past steps dim while the current one gently pulses, the block fades into the first words of the reply, a caret blinks while the answer streams, and the waiting animation changes shape with every reply. If you switch tabs while LIA works, the tab title alternates with “✦ LIA is writing…”. Everything respects your system's reduce-motion preference.

q7.question: How do I get better results with LIA?
q7.answer:
Here are the best practices for communicating with LIA:

✅ Be specific:
❌ "Find an email"
✅ "Find emails from Peter about the budget"

✅ Give context:
❌ "Send an email"
✅ "Send an email to mary@example.com to confirm the meeting tomorrow at 2pm"

✅ Use specific dates:
❌ "The meeting the other day"
✅ "The meeting on January 15"

✅ Proceed step by step:
For complex tasks, break down into multiple requests.

✅ Check previews:
Before approving an email or modification, carefully review the preview.

q8.question: How do I attach photos or documents to my messages?
q8.answer:
Three ways to attach files:

📎 Paperclip button:
Click the 📎 button to the left of the input area to browse your files.

🖱️ Drag and drop:
Drag files directly from your file explorer into the input area. A clear landing zone appears: "Drop your images or PDFs here".

📋 Paste from the clipboard:
Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on Mac) with a screenshot, an image or a PDF in the clipboard: the file is attached through the same pipeline as the paperclip (same limits, same preview). Paste text together with a file and both arrive.

📁 Accepted formats:
• Photos (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, HEIC) — automatically compressed
• PDF documents — text is automatically extracted

Thumbnails are displayed in the conversation. Click a thumbnail to enlarge it. LIA can analyze the visual content of images and the text of PDFs to answer your questions.

💡 Limits: maximum 5 attachments per message, 10 MB per image, 20 MB per document.

q9.question: What is the /resume command?
q9.answer:
The /resume command triggers intelligent context compaction:

What it does:
• Summarizes old conversation history using AI
• Preserves critical identifiers (names, emails, IDs)
• Frees up context window space for longer conversations

When to use it:
• When your conversation has been going on for a long time
• When LIA seems to lose track of earlier context
• When you want to "reset" the context without losing important information

How it works:
1. Type /resume in the chat
2. LIA summarizes old messages into a concise recap
3. Recent messages are preserved intact
4. LIA confirms the compaction with a brief summary

💡 While compaction runs:
• A toast appears at the top of the screen reading "Summarizing the conversation…"
• The input area is locked automatically while the summary completes
• When done, the toast morphs into a confirmation "Conversation summarized — N tokens freed"
• If the summary cannot complete (LLM outage, timeout), an explicit fallback cleanly truncates the older history with a visible notice rather than a silent loss

📊 Persistent indicator: A discreet pill in the chat header (next to the search box) continuously shows your tokens/threshold usage as a coloured ring — you can see at any moment when the next compaction will fire.

💡 Note: Compaction also triggers automatically when the conversation becomes very long. The /resume command lets you force it at any time.

q10.question: What is the difference between Pipeline (🔀) and ReAct (⚡) mode?
q10.answer:
LIA offers two execution modes, switchable via the 🔀/⚡ toggle in the chat header:

🔀 Pipeline mode (default)
LIA plans all steps upfront, validates them, then executes tools in parallel. This is the fastest and most economical mode: it consumes 4 to 8 times fewer tokens than ReAct mode.

⚡ ReAct mode
LIA reasons step by step: it calls a tool, analyzes the result, then autonomously decides what to do next. More adaptable and autonomous, but consumes significantly more tokens.

💡 When to use which mode?
• Pipeline (🔀): for most requests — emails, calendar, weather, contacts, tasks...
• ReAct (⚡): for exploratory research, complex multi-step questions, or when you need LIA to adapt in real time to results.

⚠️ Cost warning: ReAct mode consumes 4 to 8× more tokens. Reserve it for requests where the added value justifies the extra cost.

q11.question: How do I copy a message, code, and are math formulas rendered correctly?
q11.answer:
Since v1.16.9, the chat has several useful finishing touches:

📋 Copy button on messages and code
• Hover over a LIA reply or a code block → a "Copy" button appears
• Text is copied as-is to your clipboard, with visual confirmation

📤 Share or export an answer
• A "…" menu next to the copy button, at the bottom of every answer
• Share hands the text to your device's share sheet (Messages, Mail, Notes…) — offered only when the browser provides one
• Download as Markdown everywhere: a dated file, accents preserved

🎨 Syntax highlighting on code
• Code blocks ```python, ```typescript, ```json, ```bash, ```sql... are auto-colored (25 languages)
• Light or dark theme based on your display preferences

🧮 Math formulas (LaTeX)
• Formulas are rendered with proper mathematical notation
• Inline: $E = mc^2$
• Centered block: $$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$

📅 Relative dates
• Today's messages: time only (14:30)
• Yesterday's: "Yesterday 14:30"
• This week: weekday + time (Monday 14:30)
• Beyond: full date

q12.question: Can I search through my conversation history?
q12.answer:
Yes, since v1.16.9:

🔍 Search bar in the chat
• A search input now appears in the chat header (🔍 icon)
• Type a word or phrase → matching messages are filtered instantly
• Search is case-insensitive ("pizza" also finds "Pizza")

💡 Current limitations
• Searches through messages that are currently loaded in the chat — by default the last 50, but you can load more by scrolling up (see the next question)
• Accent-sensitive ("reunion" won't find "réunion")
• Click ✕ to clear the search and see all messages again

🎯 When to use it?
Find an address, a name, a decision or a detail mentioned earlier in the conversation without scrolling.

q13.question: How do I access older messages in a very long conversation?
q13.answer:
Since v1.20.14, you can scroll up in the chat to reach the beginning of any conversation, even one that has grown to thousands of messages:

📜 How it works
• When you open a conversation, the 50 newest messages are loaded instantly
• Scroll up in the chat — as soon as you reach the top, the previous 50 messages load automatically
• A small "Loading older messages…" indicator appears briefly at the top during each fetch
• Repeat as needed — you can scroll all the way back to the very first message

✨ What stays smooth
• Your reading position is preserved — the viewport stays exactly where you were, the new content slides in above without jumping
• Duplicates are filtered out, so no message ever appears twice

📌 Good to know
• Messages are always preserved in the database — nothing is ever lost, even after compaction (which only summarises older messages for the AI's working memory, not the displayed history)
• The in-chat search continues to filter on what's currently loaded, so loading more messages also expands the searchable scope
• Returning to the conversation later, switching tabs, or running a scheduled action all reload the newest page from scratch — so you start fresh at the bottom

q14.question: What happens if I leave the page while LIA is answering?
q14.answer:
Nothing is lost. Generation continues in the background on the server: your message and the full answer are saved even if you close the tab, switch apps or lose the connection.

When you come back to the chat while the answer is still being written, it resumes live automatically — the in-progress bubble rebuilds itself and keeps streaming (this also works with several tabs open).

You can also stop an in-progress answer: while LIA is writing, the send button becomes a Stop button. The partial text is kept and marked "interrupted" ⏸ — but note that actions already performed (a sent email, a created event…) are not undone.

Only one answer runs at a time per conversation: if you try to send another message during a generation, LIA reattaches you to the answer in progress.

q15.question: How do I approve or cancel an action LIA proposes?
q15.answer:
When LIA is about to do something sensitive (send an email, delete an event, validate a draft…), an approval card appears above the input with Confirm and Cancel buttons — and Modify for drafts, which lets you describe the change to make.

It's a single click, but you can also reply by text or voice as before (“yes, send it” / “no, cancel”): both work in parallel. Once the action is handled, the card disappears and LIA's reply confirms what was done.

q16.question: Can I see what LIA did to produce an answer?
q16.answer:
Yes. Under each answer, a small “⚙ N steps · X s” line summarizes the backstage; one click expands it to show what LIA actually did — the routing, the tools it called, and its reasoning — grouped by category.

It's the same transparency as the cost shown on every message, extended to the flow of actions. The display stays discreet and collapsed by default, so it never clutters the conversation.

Since v1.25.12 this trace is stored with the message: you will find it after a reload and on your other devices (the live reasoning stream itself stays ephemeral).

q17.question: How do I search my entire conversation history?
q17.answer:
Type in the search field of the chat header (or tap the 🔍 icon on mobile). The loaded messages filter instantly — accent-insensitive — with the matches highlighted in the bubbles and a result counter.

If older history exists, a « Search entire history » button queries the server across everything ever said and lists dated results; clicking one jumps to that moment of the conversation, and a banner offers « Back to present » at any time. Sending a new message automatically returns you to the present first.

q18.question: What are the 👍/👎 under the responses for?
q18.answer:
Two discreet thumbs appear next to the Copy button on ordinary responses. Your verdict is saved with the message (you will find it on your other devices) and feeds LIA's understanding: it strengthens or weakens the personal observations that shaped that answer. A 👎 unfolds an optional one-line « what went wrong? » field, recorded as a correction.

You can change your mind — the latest verdict wins. And LIA never regenerates an answer on its own: you stay in charge.

q19.question: Can LIA prepare me before talking to someone? (v1.25.13)
q19.answer:
Yes — ask « prepare my call with Marie » and one pass gathers a 360° view: her contact card, your recent email exchanges, your upcoming shared meetings, and what LIA remembers about her. If a source is unavailable (no calendar connector, for instance), the overview says so honestly instead of guessing.

It also powers the meeting-prep nudge: when a substantial meeting is close, a proactive notification may end with « want me to prepare this meeting for you? ».

q20.question: What are the « / » slash commands? (v1.25.16)
q20.answer: Type / at the start of an empty message to open the command menu: /resume (compact the conversation), /briefing (open the dashboard), /agenda, /search, plus everyday shortcuts — unread emails, weather, weekend weather, tasks, reminders, news — and your dialogue-enabled skills. Filtering understands your language (typing « mété » finds the weather). A command only pre-fills the input: nothing is ever sent without you pressing Enter.

q21.question: Does my typed message survive a refresh? Can I recall what I sent? (v1.25.16)
q21.answer: Yes. Your draft is saved per account as you type and restored after a refresh or navigation (it is cleared when you send, and purged at logout). In an empty input, ↑ walks back through your last 10 sent messages and ↓ walks forward to an empty field — like a terminal. Under every answer, an action row offers copy, feedback (👍/👎) and the execution details (« N steps · X s »).

q22.question: The thread no longer jumps while I re-read — how does it work? (v1.25.16)
q22.answer: When you scroll up to re-read, a streaming answer never drags you back to the bottom. A floating button appears with a counter of the responses that arrived off-screen; one tap brings you back. Sending a message still jumps to it, as expected. Under the latest answer, up to 3 follow-up suggestions may appear as chips: tapping one fills the input (never sends).

q23.question: A message failed — do I have to retype my question?
q23.answer:
No. An error bubble now carries a Retry button, and it replays exactly the request that failed.

Why that precision matters:
Between your question and your click, LIA may have sent you a proactive notification. Replaying "the last message" would then send something other than what you asked for. The question is therefore pinned to the failure bubble at the moment it happens.

💡 Good to know:
A failure with no preceding question (a notification, for instance) shows no button: there would be nothing to replay.

q24.question: What happens when LIA cannot carry out my request?
q24.answer:
LIA drafts a plan before acting, then re-reads it before running it. When that plan writes something — sending an email, creating an appointment, calling someone — and it cannot repair the plan on its own, it refuses to run it and asks you a question. Writing wrong data costs more than asking.

The question is written in your language and says exactly what is missing: which recipient, which date, which items to act on. It never contains technical jargon, a code path or an example address — what LIA shows you is a question, not its internal diagnosis.

You can answer, rephrase, or drop it: nothing is sent until you decide.

q25.question: What are the little animated eyes on the chat page?
q25.answer:
They are LIA's expressive eyes — a small companion widget that mirrors what the assistant is doing and feeling. They watch the input while you type, squint while LIA thinks, scan side to side while it searches, and play the register of each answer — LIA states whether what she has just written is warm, assured, factual, apologetic, curious or concerned, and the face plays it, mouth included. Twelve distinct expressions, only two of which smile: a technical answer keeps a focused face. Left alone they blink, glance around, doze off, and occasionally pull a prank.

Make them yours: drag them anywhere (arrow keys work too, and they never drift from where you put them), tap them on mobile to reveal the size and hide buttons, or dismiss them to a small restore dot. Six visual styles are available in Settings › Personalization › Eyes style, with live previews. Under reduced-motion system settings the eyes stay still.

q1.question: How do I change my timezone?
q1.answer:
The timezone affects how dates and times are displayed in your conversations:

To change it:
1. Go to Settings (⚙️ icon in the menu)
2. In the rail, under Preferences › Personalization, pick Timezone
3. It opens in the panel beside the rail — choose yours

🌍 Automatic detection:
On your first login, LIA detects your timezone from your browser.

💡 Traveler tip:
If you travel, LIA notices the mismatch with your browser and offers to update your timezone in one click.

q2.question: How do I change the interface language?
q2.answer:
Two ways to change the language:

Quick method:
Click the globe icon 🌐 in the title bar and pick your language.

Via settings:
1. Go to Settings (⚙️ icon in the menu)
2. In the rail, under Preferences › Personalization, pick Language
3. It opens in the panel beside the rail

🔄 Sync:
Both methods save the same preference to your profile, so it follows you across devices.

📧 Beyond the interface:
Notification emails and the push notifications LIA sends you also use this language.

q3.question: How do I customize appearance (themes)?
q3.answer:
Customize LIA's appearance to your taste:

5 themes available:
• 💙 Professional Blue: elegant and timeless
• 🌊 Teal: deep teal, sophisticated and calming
• 🌿 Sage: modern sage green, natural and organic
• 🌹 Rose: dusty rose, elegant and warm
• 💜 Lavender: soft lavender, refined and creative

Light, dark, absolute black:
Each theme exists in a light and a dark version, and dark has two depths — ordinary dark, and absolute black for OLED screens, where those pixels really switch off. The button in the title bar cycles through the three, and its icon shows where the next press goes. In Settings › Appearance you can also pick the mode directly, including System (follow your device), with an Absolute black switch available once dark is selected.

To change theme:
Go to Settings (⚙️ icon) and find the Theme section.

q4.question: How do I update my profile?
q4.answer:
Manage your personal information:

Editable:
• ✏️ Full name: the name shown in the app — Settings > Profile
• 🌍 Timezone, 🌐 Language, 🎨 Appearance: Settings > Preferences, under Personalization

Not editable:
• 📧 Email: it is your login identifier and is fixed after registration

💡 Good to know:
Your name is what LIA uses to address you, so a nickname works just as well as a legal name.

q5.question: How do I customize LIA's style?

14 available personalities:

• Influencer: trendy and engaging style
• Philosopher: reflective and insightful

• Poet: lyrical and imaginative expression
• Coach: motivational and action-oriented
• And more — administrators can add new ones!

🌍 6 languages:
Each personality is automatically translated into French, English, Spanish, German, Italian and Chinese.

Two methods to change:
• Quick method: click the ✨ icon in the title bar
• Via settings: go to Settings (⚙️ icon), Personality section

💡 Tip: Try different styles to find the one that suits you best!

q6.question: Are my preferences synchronized?
q6.answer:
Yes, all your preferences are automatically synchronized:

🔄 What's synchronized:
• Interface language
• Timezone
• Theme and light/dark mode
• LIA personality style
• Voice preferences
• Active connectors
• Default calendar and task preferences

📱 Multi-device:
Your preferences follow you on all devices. Change the theme on mobile, find it on your computer.

💾 Instant save:
Each change is recorded immediately.

q7.question: How do I enable or disable LIA's voice?
q7.answer:
LIA has a bidirectional voice system:

🔊 Voice Synthesis (TTS) - LIA speaks to you:
Click the speaker icon 🔊 in the title bar. When enabled, LIA reads its responses aloud.
• Standard (default): Microsoft Edge TTS - free
• HD: OpenAI or Gemini TTS - premium quality (if enabled by administrator)

🎙️ Voice Mode (STT) - Speak to LIA:
Hold the voice badge in the chat header for 500ms to enable voice mode.
• Wake word: Say 'OK Guy' or 'OK Guys' to activate recording
• Push-to-talk: Click the overlay to speak manually
• Auto-detection: LIA detects when you stop speaking (1s silence)
• Free and offline: Transcription uses Whisper locally

💡 Tip:
Voice mode is ideal for hands-free use or multitasking.

q8.question: How do I change LIA's voice (male/female)?
q8.answer:
Choose the voice gender that suits you:

🎙️ Available voices:
• Female: soft and natural neural voice
• Male: deep and calm neural voice

To change:
1. Go to the Dashboard (home screen)
2. Click on the assistant's image (LIA's avatar)
3. The image changes to reflect the new gender
4. The voice automatically switches between female and male

🌍 Automatic language:
The voice automatically adapts to the interface language. For example, a French voice if the interface is in French.

⚙️ Quality:
LIA uses high-quality neural voices (Microsoft Edge TTS in standard mode, or OpenAI/Gemini TTS in HD mode) for a natural and expressive rendering.

q9.question: How does long-term memory work?
q9.answer:
LIA learns about you through its intelligent memory:

🧠 What LIA remembers:
• Preferences: "He prefers concise emails", "She likes black coffee"
• Personal information: "His birthday is March 15"
• Relationships: "Mary is his sister", "John is his colleague"
• Significant events: "He changed jobs recently"
• Habits: "She exercises on Tuesday evenings"
• Sensitive areas: topics to approach with care

🔄 Automatic extraction:
LIA analyzes your conversations and automatically extracts relevant information in the background.

🔍 Dual semantic search:
Each memory is indexed twice — once on its content, once on the keywords that trigger it. Your question is compared to both, and the better match wins, so a memory is found whether you phrase it the way it was recorded or not.

📊 Usage:
These memories personalize LIA's responses. For example, LIA will say "Hello Mary" to your sister without you specifying.

🛡️ Full control:
View, edit, pin or delete your memories in Settings > Memory.

q10.question: How do I manage my stored memories?
q10.answer:
You have full control over what LIA remembers:

📋 View your memories:
Go to Settings > Long-term Memory to see everything LIA has remembered.

✏️ Edit a memory:
• Click the edit button
• Correct the content or category
• Adjust usage nuances

📌 Pin a memory:
Pinned memories are protected from automatic cleanup. Useful for important information.

🗑️ Delete:
• Delete individually or in bulk
• Option to keep pinned memories

📤 Export:
Export all your memories for backup (GDPR compliance).

🔄 Automatic cleanup:
Unpinned memories are automatically purged based on a retention score (importance, recency and actual usage) to keep the system relevant.

⚠️ Forgetting risk:
Memories close to being automatically forgotten are flagged in the list, so you can pin the ones that matter in time.

q11.question: How do I configure my geolocation and home address?
q11.answer:
LIA can use your geographic location for contextual searches:

📍 Home address:
1. Go to Settings > Preferences > Location
2. Enter your address in the Home address field
3. Validate to save

🎯 Usage:
• "Restaurants near me" will use your address
• "Weather here" will show your home's weather
• "Pharmacies nearby" will search around your address

🌐 Browser geolocation:
You can also allow real-time geolocation via your browser for even more accurate results.

🔒 Privacy:
Your address is stored securely and only used for your proximity queries.

q12.question: How does LIA resolve relational references?
q12.answer:
LIA understands references to your loved ones through its memory:

👥 Reference examples:
• "Send an email to my brother" → LIA finds the corresponding contact
• "What did my wife send me?" → searches your emails
• "Call my doctor" → finds Dr. X's contact

🔗 How it works:
1. LIA extracts relationships from your conversations ("My brother's name is John")
2. These associations are stored in your long-term memory
3. During a query, LIA automatically resolves "my brother" to "John Smith"

✏️ Customize relationships:
You can create or modify these associations in Settings > Long-term Memory.

💡 Tip:
Mention your relationships naturally in conversations: "My colleague Sophie sent me a file".

q13.question: How do I view my token consumption in chat?
q13.answer:
You can display consumption metrics in real-time during your conversations:

💰 To enable/disable display:
Click the dollar icon 💲 in the title bar (available on desktop only).

📊 Information displayed:
When enabled, each LIA message shows:
• Input tokens: your message + analyzed context
• Output tokens: the response generated by LIA
• Cached tokens: reused data (savings)
• Estimated cost: in euros for this message
• Conversation total: cumulative since start

💡 Why is this useful?
• Understand what consumes resources
• Optimize your requests if needed
• Track your usage in real-time

📱 Note:
This feature is not available on mobile due to display space constraints.

q14.question: Which languages are supported for voice transcription?

🌍 Main languages:

🔄 Automatic detection:

q15.question: Voice mode isn't working, what should I do?
q15.answer:
Here are solutions to common voice mode issues:

🎤 Microphone problem:
1. Check that your browser has permission to use the microphone
2. Click the 🔒 icon to the left of the URL to see permissions
3. Allow the microphone if blocked

🌐 Unsupported browser:
Voice mode requires a modern browser:
• ✅ Chrome 92+
• ✅ Firefox 79+
• ✅ Safari 15.2+
• ✅ Edge 92+
• ❌ Internet Explorer (not supported)

🔒 Security headers:
Voice mode uses advanced features (SharedArrayBuffer) that require security headers. If you see a "crossOriginIsolated" error, contact the administrator.

🔇 Wake word not detected:
• Say "OK Guy" or "OK Guys" clearly
• Avoid noisy environments
• Get closer to the microphone
• Use Push-to-Talk (click the overlay) as an alternative

⏱️ Slow transcription:
The first transcription may take 2-3 seconds (model loading). Subsequent ones are faster (~500ms).

q16.question: How do I export my consumption data?
q16.answer:
You can export your personal LLM and Google API consumption as CSV files:

📥 To export:
1. Go to Settings > Features
2. Open the My Consumption Export section
3. Choose a date range (current month, last month, last 30 days, or all time)
4. Click Download CSV on the export you want

📊 Three export types:
• LLM Token Usage — Detailed per-call breakdown (model, tokens, cost)
• Google API Usage — Detailed per-call breakdown (API, endpoint, cost)
• My Summary — Aggregated totals (tokens, calls, costs)

🔒 Security:
You can only export your own data. It is not possible to access other users' consumption data.

q17.question: Can I customize the dashboard cards? (v1.25.16)
q17.answer: Yes — the shortest path: the "Customize" button next to "Refresh all", right above the grid, leads straight to the right section. Or go through Settings → « My dashboard ». Hide any of the 9 briefing cards or reorder them (↑/↓ buttons, or drag-and-drop). A hidden card is not even fetched anymore: fewer API calls, faster dashboard. A starter checklist on the dashboard also shows what your instance can do (connectors, voice, channels…) until you dismiss it.

q18.question: What is the « Commitments » section? (v1.25.16)
q18.answer: LIA automatically detects commitments in your conversations (« I must call the plumber back », « waiting for Marc's reply »). Settings → Features → « Commitments » lists them by direction (you owe / you are waiting), with three one-tap actions: Done, Relaunch in chat (pre-fills a follow-up message) or No longer relevant. Nothing is created manually — the ledger's value is being automatic. The same actions are available from a relation's sheet, and a commitment's wording or deadline can be corrected — correcting is not creating: the ledger stays automatic, it simply stops being wrong.

q19.question: How do I find a setting quickly?
q19.answer:
The settings page lists every section in a rail that never scrolls away, and opens the one you pick in the panel beside it. The "Search a setting" field, at the top of the rail, takes you straight there.

What the search understands:
• The title and description of every section
• Translated synonyms: "dark" for Appearance, "2FA" or "TOTP" for Strong authentication, "GDPR" for your data export, "cron" for Scheduled actions
• Accents and apostrophes are ignored — "theme" finds "Thème"

When you pick a result:
LIA opens the section in the panel and brings the cursor to it. Everything works from the keyboard — arrows to walk, Enter to open, Escape to dismiss — and the number of matches is announced to screen readers.

Before you search at all:
Each family of settings has its own colour and each setting its own icon, on the home cards as in the rail — so a section you have already visited is found by its look, not by reading. The colour groups and decorates: it never carries an information on its own, and the section you have open is still marked by its background and its accent.

Some sections only exist when the feature is active on your account: LIA then tells you so, rather than leaving you in front of a page that did not move.

q20.question: Where can I see everything LIA sent me, without digging through settings?
q20.answer: The Alerts destination in the navigation bar gathers five streams in one screen: relayed peer messages, proactive notifications, interest notifications, pending reminders and scheduled routines. Each section arrives folded already showing its exact count — you choose what to open without having to open it to find out — and paginates by ten. No list is fetched until something is unfolded: only the counts are, in a single read. The settings panels remain the detailed configuration for each of those streams, and every link you had saved keeps working.

q21.question: How does an administrator update the LLM model prices in bulk?
q21.answer:
From Settings → Administration → LLM pricing, the whole catalogue — every model, every characteristic, every tariff — downloads as a structured Excel workbook, and the edited file goes back in the same way.

What the workbook contains: a usage notice translated into your language, one row per model with dropdown lists and cell validations, a referentials sheet feeding those lists, a sheet listing the UTC time windows for providers that bill peak/off-peak hours, and a status column stating what would really happen — no active tariff (billed zero), several active tariffs, or billed under another model's name.

Re-importing happens in two steps. The file is analysed and the whole diff is shown field by field — created, updated, reactivated, retired — while nothing is written yet; only then can it be applied, and only against the preview you read.

What an import can never do: a row missing from the file never deletes anything (a forgotten Excel filter cannot empty the catalogue — removal is declared explicitly by setting the is_active column to false, and setting it back to true brings the model back); anything unreadable or contradictory is reported with the sheet and the cell to fix and the import writes nothing at all; a tariff is rewritten only if it actually changed, so re-importing an untouched file leaves the price history exactly as it was; and if someone else changed a model between the preview and the confirmation, only the affected rows are refused, not the whole file.

Reasoning is written in the workbook. Two columns carry it: whether the model reasons, and the depths it accepts, comma-separated. A third, read-only, restates the family LIA recognised and the ladder it will apply. On re-import, a depth that family does not offer is refused while naming the ones that would have been accepted — a spreadsheet cannot render checkboxes, so the check happens at import time.

q22.question: How do I choose how deeply a model thinks?
q22.answer:
In Settings → Administration → LLM Pricing, open a model: LIA shows the depths that model actually accepts — from "no thinking" up to "maximum" — and you untick the ones it refuses. Leaving everything ticked means "no restriction": its family's full ladder applies.

You therefore never type a level, and you cannot write one that does not exist. The list comes from the same source the server validates against: what the screen offers is exactly what the model's API accepts.

If no known family matches the model, LIA says so plainly rather than showing an empty list: no thinking parameter will be sent for it, and teaching LIA one is a code change.

The depth actually used for each role (routing, planning, answering…) is set in LLM Configuration, where the same resolved list is offered.

q1.question: What is a connector?
q1.answer:
A connector is a secure gateway between LIA and your external services:

🔌 Types of connectors:

Google Services (OAuth):
• 📧 Gmail: read, send, reply to emails
• 📅 Calendar: manage your events
• 👥 Contacts: search and create contacts
• 📁 Drive: explore your files
• ✅ Tasks: manage your tasks
• 📍 Places: search for locations
• 🗺️ Routes: directions and routes

Apple iCloud services (app-specific password):
• 📮 Apple Mail: read, send, reply to emails (IMAP/SMTP)
• 🗓️ Apple Calendar: manage your iCloud events (CalDAV)
• 📇 Apple Contacts: search and create iCloud contacts (CardDAV)

Microsoft 365 services (OAuth):
• 📧 Outlook: read, send, reply to emails
• 📅 Microsoft Calendar: manage your events
• 👥 Microsoft Contacts: search and manage contacts
• ✅ Microsoft To Do: manage tasks and lists

External services (API key):
• 🌤️ OpenWeatherMap: weather and forecasts
• 📚 Wikipedia: encyclopedic search
• 🔍 Perplexity: AI web search
• 🦁 Brave Search: web and news enrichment

Smart Home (hybrid auth):
• 💡 Philips Hue: control lights, rooms, and scenes

Telephony (bring-your-own):
• 📞 ElevenLabs Telephony: LIA places outbound phone calls on your behalf — see the dedicated Phone Calls section

🔒 Security:
Each connector has limited permissions. LIA only accesses necessary data.

⚡ Mutual exclusivity:
For email, calendar, and contacts, only one provider can be active at a time (Google OR Apple OR Microsoft, not both simultaneously). Tasks are available via Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do (one at a time).

q2.question: How do I connect Google services?
q2.answer:
Google services use OAuth 2.0 (secure connection):

Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. Find the desired service (Gmail, Calendar, etc.)
3. Click Connect
4. A Google window opens
5. Select your Google account
6. Accept the requested permissions
7. You're redirected to LIA - the connector is active!

🔐 Permissions:
LIA only requests necessary permissions. For example, for Gmail: reading and sending emails, but not permanent deletion.

💡 Tip:
You can revoke access at any time from LIA settings or from your Google account.

q3.question: How do I connect external services (API key)?
q3.answer:
Some services require a personal API key:

🌤️ OpenWeatherMap (free):
1. Create an account at openweathermap.org
2. Get your free API key
3. In LIA: Settings > Connectors > OpenWeatherMap
4. Paste your key and click Activate

🔍 Perplexity (paid):
1. Create an account at perplexity.ai
2. Subscribe to an API plan
3. Get your API key
4. Activate in LIA as above

📚 Wikipedia:
No key required! Wikipedia is free and directly accessible.

🔒 Key security:
Your API keys are stored securely and encrypted.

q4.question: How do I disconnect a service?
q4.answer:
To revoke LIA's access to a service:

Disconnection from LIA:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. Find the service to disconnect
3. Click Disconnect
4. Confirm disconnection

⚠️ Consequences:
• LIA will no longer be able to access this service
• Your data remains intact with the provider (Google, etc.)
• You can reconnect at any time

🔐 Double security (Google):
For Google services, you can also revoke access from:
• myaccount.google.com/permissions
• This disconnects LIA immediately

q5.question: Why is a connector showing an error?
q5.answer:
Several reasons can explain a connector error:

🔄 Expired token:
Solution: Click Reconnect to refresh the authorization.

🚫 Permissions revoked:
If you revoked access from Google, reconnect.

🔑 Invalid API key:
For API key services, verify your key is correct and active.

⏱️ Quota exceeded:
Some services have usage limits. Wait or upgrade to a higher plan.

🌐 Network issue:
Check your internet connection and try again.

💡 General solution:
Disconnect then reconnect the service. This solves most problems.

q6.question: Can I configure preferences per connector?
q6.answer:
Yes! Some connectors have customizable preferences:

📅 Google Calendar:
• Default calendar: where to create new events
• Example: "Work", "Personal", "Family"
• LIA will use this calendar unless specified otherwise

✅ Google Tasks:
• Default task list: where to create new tasks
• Example: "My main list", "Projects", "Shopping"

📍 Location:
• Home address: your default address for "near me" searches
• Automatic geolocation: send your position for accurate results
• Location memory (opt-in): remember your last position so LIA keeps answering from where you are when the live position is unavailable — always announced with its age, never presented as current, encrypted and erased the moment you switch it off
• Configure all three in Settings > Preferences > Location — this data lives on your account, not on a connector

🌐 Browser Geolocation:
• In the Location section (Settings > Preferences), enable the geolocation toggle
• Your browser will ask for permission the first time
• Position used for local weather and "near me" searches
• On mobile, the position refreshes silently when you return to the app; if the system dropped the permission, a chat banner offers to re-enable it

To configure:
1. Go to Settings (⚙️ icon in the menu)
2. Open the Connectors section
3. Find the relevant connector (Calendar or Tasks)
4. Configure the specific preferences for that connector

💡 Tip:
These preferences save you time by not having to specify the calendar, list, or city each time.

q7.question: Which Google services can I connect?
q7.answer:
LIA integrates with 7 Google services:

📧 Gmail
• Search all your emails
• Read message content
• Send, reply, forward
• View attachments

📅 Google Calendar
• View your schedule
• Create events
• Modify or delete
• Invite participants

👥 Google Contacts
• Search by name, email, company
• Create new contacts
• Update information

📁 Google Drive
• Search your files
• Read document content
• Browse folders

✅ Google Tasks
• List your tasks
• Create new tasks
• Mark as completed

📍 Google Places
• Search for locations
• Get addresses and hours
• View reviews

🗺️ Google Routes
• Calculate routes
• Compare transport modes
• Estimate travel times

q8.question: Are connectors secure?
q8.answer:
Security is our top priority:

🔐 Google services — OAuth 2.0:
• LIA never sees your Google passwords
• You connect directly with Google
• Tokens revocable at any time

🍎 Apple services — App-specific password:
• Uses an application-specific password (not your Apple password)
• Encrypted before database storage
• Revocable from appleid.apple.com
• Apple two-factor authentication is required

🪟 Microsoft 365 — OAuth 2.0:
• LIA never sees your Microsoft passwords
• You connect directly with Microsoft
• Tokens revocable at any time from your Microsoft account
• Limited permissions (Microsoft Graph API)

🔒 Minimal permissions:
• Each connector only requests necessary permissions
• No excessive access to your data

🗄️ Secure storage:
• OAuth tokens and app-specific passwords encrypted in database
• API keys stored securely
• No plaintext storage

🔄 Automatic refresh:
• Google and Microsoft tokens expire regularly and are renewed automatically
• Apple app-specific passwords don't expire (unless Apple ID password changes)

📋 Audit and logs:
• All actions are tracked
• Usage history available

q9.question: How do I connect Apple iCloud services?
q9.answer:
Apple iCloud services use an app-specific password:

Prerequisites:
• An Apple account with two-factor authentication enabled
• Generate an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com

Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. In the Apple iCloud section, click Connect
3. Enter your Apple ID (email)
4. Enter the app-specific password (format xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx)
5. Select the services to activate (Email, Calendar, Contacts)
6. Click Test connection to verify
7. Click Activate

⚠️ Mutual exclusivity:
Activating an Apple service automatically deactivates its Google equivalent (and vice versa). For example, activating Apple Mail will deactivate Gmail.

🔐 Security:
Your app-specific password is encrypted and never exposed. You can revoke it at any time from your Apple account.

q10.question: What Apple iCloud services can I connect?
q10.answer:
LIA integrates with 3 Apple iCloud services:

📮 Apple Mail (IMAP/SMTP)
• Search your iCloud emails
• Read message content
• Send, reply, forward
• View attachments
• Navigate by IMAP folders

🗓️ Apple Calendar (CalDAV)
• View your iCloud calendar
• Create events
• Modify or delete
• Invite participants

📇 Apple Contacts (CardDAV)
• Search by name, email, company
• Create new contacts
• Update information

❌ Not available:
• Apple Reminders: Apple doesn't provide a standard API for accessing Reminders from a server. Tasks remain available via Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do.

💡 Same experience:
Commands are identical whether you use Google or Apple. Just say "my emails", "my calendar", or "my contacts" — LIA automatically uses the active provider.

q11.question: What is connector mutual exclusivity?
q11.answer:
For email, calendar, contacts, and tasks services, LIA applies a mutual exclusivity rule:

⚡ Principle:
Only one provider can be active per category:
• Email: Gmail OR Apple Mail OR Outlook (not multiple)
• Calendar: Google Calendar OR Apple Calendar OR Microsoft Calendar (not multiple)
• Contacts: Google Contacts OR Apple Contacts OR Microsoft Contacts (not multiple)
• Tasks: Google Tasks OR Microsoft To Do (not both)

🔄 Switching providers:
If you activate a new provider while another is active for the same category:
1. The previous service becomes inactive (not deleted)
2. The new service becomes active
3. Your data remains intact with each provider
4. You can switch back at any time

✅ Unaffected services:
Google Drive, Places, Routes, and Philips Hue have no equivalent in other providers and remain always available.

💡 Tip:
You don't need to choose the same provider for everything. For example, you can use Outlook for emails, Google Calendar for your calendar, and Microsoft To Do for tasks.

q12.question: How do I connect Microsoft 365 services?
q12.answer:
Microsoft 365 services use OAuth 2.0 (secure connection via Microsoft Identity Platform):

Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. In the Microsoft 365 section, click Connect All or select an individual service
3. A Microsoft login window opens
4. Sign in with your Microsoft account
5. Accept the requested permissions
6. You're redirected back to LIA — the connector is active!

🔐 Permissions:
LIA only requests necessary permissions via the Microsoft Graph API. For example, for Outlook: reading and sending emails, but not permanent deletion.

⚠️ Mutual exclusivity:
Activating a Microsoft service automatically deactivates its Google or Apple equivalent for the same category (and vice versa).

💡 Tip:
You can revoke access at any time from LIA settings or from account.microsoft.com.

q13.question: What Microsoft 365 services can I connect?
q13.answer:
LIA integrates with 4 Microsoft 365 services:

📧 Outlook (Microsoft Graph)
• Search your emails
• Read message content
• Send, reply, forward
• View attachments

📅 Microsoft Calendar
• View your schedule
• Create events
• Modify or delete
• Invite participants

👥 Microsoft Contacts
• Search by name, email, company
• Create new contacts
• Update information

✅ Microsoft To Do
• List your tasks
• Create new tasks
• Mark as completed
• Manage task lists

💡 Same experience:
Commands are identical regardless of provider. Just say "my emails", "my calendar", "my contacts", or "my tasks" — LIA automatically uses the active provider.

q14.question: How do I connect Philips Hue?
q14.answer:
Philips Hue uses hybrid authentication (local press-link or remote OAuth2):

🏠 Local mode (recommended — same network):
1. Go to Settings > Smart Home > Philips Hue
2. Click Local connection
3. Click Search for bridges
4. Select your bridge
5. Press the physical button on top of your Hue Bridge
6. Click Pair within 30 seconds
7. LIA validates connectivity and activates the connector

🌐 Remote mode (different network):
1. Configure Hue Remote API credentials on the server
2. Click Remote connection
3. Authorize LIA via Philips OAuth2

💡 What you can do:
• "Turn on the living room lights"
• "Dim the bedroom to 30%"
• "Set the kitchen light to blue"
• "Activate the movie scene"
• "What lights are currently on?"
• "Turn off everything"

⚡ 6 tools available:
List lights, control a light (on/off, brightness, color), list rooms, control a room, list scenes, activate a scene.

telephony.title: Phone Calls
telephony.description: LIA can place real phone calls on your behalf. Complete setup guide (Twilio + ElevenLabs) and everyday use.

q1.question: What can LIA do on the phone?
q1.answer:
LIA can place a real outbound phone call for you, pursue the goal you set, and report back in the chat.

Examples:
• "Call the bakery and ask if they have a cake for Saturday"
• "Call the garage to check if the car is ready"
• "Call Marie and ask if she's free Tuesday evening"

During the call, LIA introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf, holds a natural conversation toward your objective, then hangs up and writes you a summary — with a one-tap follow-up action when relevant (for example, creating the event that was just agreed).

💡 Good to know: LIA only places outgoing calls — it never answers your incoming calls.

q2.question: How does a call work, step by step?
q2.answer:
1. You ask in the chat
"Call Dr. Martin's office and ask for an appointment this week"

2. LIA asks for your confirmation
Before dialing anything, LIA shows you a confirmation card: who it will call, which number, and why. Nothing happens without your explicit approval.

3. The call takes place
LIA's voice agent makes the call from your number and works toward the objective. You can keep chatting with LIA — or close the app — in the meantime.

4. The summary arrives in the chat
A written summary is delivered asynchronously, with a suggested follow-up action when there is something to do next. Every call also appears in your call history (Settings > Connectors > Telephony).

q3.question: What do I need before starting?
q3.answer:
Phone calls use your own accounts with two external services — LIA adds no charge of its own:

1. 📞 A Twilio account — provides the phone number LIA calls from (number rental + per-minute pricing).

2. 🎙️ An ElevenLabs account — provides the voice agent that speaks during the call (requires access to the Agents platform; call minutes consume your plan's credits).

3. ✅ The feature enabled by your administrator — if you don't see a Telephony block in Settings > Connectors, ask your administrator to enable it.

The full setup takes about 15 minutes (plus possible validation delays for a French number) and follows 4 steps, each detailed in the next questions:
1. Get a phone number (Twilio)
2. Prepare ElevenLabs (API key + number import)
3. Configure the return webhook
4. Activate the connector in LIA

q4.question: Step 1 — Get a phone number (Twilio)
q4.answer:
Twilio is the operator that provides the number LIA calls from.

1. Create the account
Sign up at twilio.com and upgrade to a paid account (the free trial only calls verified numbers).

2. 🇫🇷 For a French number: submit a Regulatory Bundle
French regulation requires an identity document and a proof of address: Phone Numbers > Regulatory Compliance > Bundles. Human validation takes up to ~3 business days.
• Easiest: a local number (01–05) or national number (09)
• Avoid mobile numbers (06/07): extra requirements and 1–2 weeks of provisioning

3. Buy the number
Phone Numbers > Buy a Number — make sure the Voice capability is checked.

4. Note your credentials
On the Twilio Console dashboard, copy the Account SID and the Auth Token — you will need them in the next step.

💡 Just testing? A US number can be bought instantly, with no regulatory bundle.

q5.question: Step 2 — Prepare ElevenLabs (API key + number)
q5.answer:
ElevenLabs provides the voice agent that speaks during the call.

1. Check your plan
You need a plan with access to the Agents platform. Call minutes consume your ElevenLabs credits (on top of Twilio's per-minute cost).

2. Create an API key
Profile (bottom left) > API Keys > create a key. If you restrict its permissions, it needs at least read/write access to the Agents platform (LIA creates its agent, lists your numbers, and triggers outbound calls). A full-access key works fine to start — you can restrict it after your first successful call.

3. Import your Twilio number
Agents Platform > Phone Numbers > Import from Twilio: enter the number in international format (e.g. +33612345678), the Account SID, the Auth Token, and a label.

⚠️ Two important points:
• Use the native Twilio import, not a SIP trunk — LIA triggers calls through ElevenLabs' Twilio integration.
• Do not create an agent yourself: LIA automatically provisions its own secured agent when you activate the connector (it will appear in your workspace as "LIA telephony — your name").

q6.question: Step 3 — Configure the return webhook
q6.answer:
The webhook is the channel through which the call report comes back into your chat. Without it, calls go out but no summary ever returns.

1. Open the webhooks settings
In the ElevenLabs Agents workspace settings, open the Webhooks section (only a workspace admin can do this).

2. Create a post-call webhook
• Event type: post_call_transcription (transcription only)
• URL: the address LIA shows you at step 3 of its wizard, with a copy button — it looks like https://your-lia-domain/api/v1/telephony/webhook
• Authentication: HMAC

3. Copy the signing secret
ElevenLabs generates a signing secret when the webhook is created — copy it immediately, you will paste it into LIA in the next step.

🔒 Leave "Send audio data" disabled: LIA never receives nor stores any audio — that is a design guarantee.

q7.question: Step 4 — Activate the connector in LIA
q7.answer:
Everything now comes together in LIA, in a 3-step wizard.

Go to Settings > Connectors > Telephony and click Connect. A notice reminds you that calls are billed on your own ElevenLabs/Twilio accounts.

Step 1 — API key
Paste your ElevenLabs API key and click Validate. LIA checks the key and lists the phone numbers of your workspace. ("No numbers" means the Twilio import from Step 2 is missing.)

Step 2 — Number
Pick the number LIA will call from.

Step 3 — Webhook
Copy the displayed webhook URL (if you haven't configured it in ElevenLabs yet, do it now — see the previous question), paste the signing secret, and click Activate.

LIA then creates its secured agent in your ElevenLabs workspace and the connector goes active. You're ready to call! 🎉

q8.question: How do I place my first call?
q8.answer:
💡 Recommended first test: have LIA call your own mobile — you'll experience a call from the other side.

1. In the chat: "Call +336XXXXXXXX and ask whether the package has arrived"

2. LIA shows the confirmation card (callee, number, objective) — confirm.

3. Your phone rings: the agent introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf, asks its question, and hangs up.

4. The summary appears in the chat a few moments later — asynchronously, so you can chat in the meantime.

You can also target a contact by name ("call Marie…"): LIA looks up the number in your contacts and asks you to disambiguate if several match. The call history lives in Settings > Connectors > Telephony.

q9.question: Is it private? Can LIA reveal my calendar or record the call?
q9.answer:
Privacy is enforced by design, not by instructions:

• 🔒 Read-only, free/busy only — during a call LIA can check whether you're free or busy at a given time, but never reveals your event titles, participants, locations or any content. The call agent simply has no access to that data.
• 🚫 No recording — the call is not recorded.
• 🗑️ No stored transcript — the full conversation is never saved; only a short summary is kept, and it expires automatically (30 days by default).
• 📢 Transparent disclosure — the agent always introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf; it never pretends to be you.
• ✅ You stay in control — every call is confirmed by you before it is placed.

q10.question: Can the assistant accept an extra or commit to an expense for me?
q10.answer: No, never. The assistant operates under a strict mandate: it can only act within the exact scope of your request. If the person offers an extra, an option, a price change or any unplanned commitment (even a small one, like a 3€ cheese topping on a pizza), it neither accepts nor declines on your behalf: it notes the exact offer and its price, explains that it cannot confirm by itself, and announces a call-back to confirm. You then find everything in the call summary — every cost with its amount, every open point — and LIA asks you how to proceed. If you wish, just request a new call with your instructions ("call back and accept the cheese topping").

q11.question: How much does it cost?
q11.answer:
LIA adds no charge of its own — costs go to your two external accounts:

📞 Twilio
• Number rental: ~1–15 €/month depending on the type
• Outbound minutes: per-minute rate based on the destination

🎙️ ElevenLabs
• Agent call minutes, taken from your plan's credits

🤖 LIA
• No surcharge, no markup — only the small LLM synthesis of your summary appears in your LIA usage statistics.

🛡️ Built-in guardrails against surprises:
• One active call at a time
• Hourly call cap per user (10/hour by default)
• Hard cap on call duration (10 minutes by default)

q12.question: It doesn't work — what should I check?
q12.answer:
"Invalid key" at step 1
→ The key is mistyped or lacks permissions (Agents platform access required).

"No numbers" after validating the key
→ Your number isn't imported into the ElevenLabs Agents workspace, or was imported as a SIP trunk instead of the native Twilio integration.

The call goes out but no summary comes back
→ The webhook is the issue: URL not publicly reachable, wrong signing secret, or wrong event type (it must be post_call_transcription).

"A call is already in progress"
→ Only one active call at a time, by design. A stuck call is automatically cleaned up after ~15 minutes.

Calls refused after several in a row
→ You've hit the hourly cap (10 calls/hour by default).

Still stuck? Ask your administrator: the server logs state precisely which webhook events were received and why any were ignored.

q13.question: Can I follow a call while it is happening?
q13.answer:
Yes. As soon as LIA starts dialling, a banner appears above the conversation: who she is calling, and where the call stands. It disappears the moment the call ends.

📒 Afterwards:
The history lives in Settings → Preferences → Recent calls: name, objective, status, outcome and recap. Never the number — the API does not expose it. The section does not appear at all if you have never placed a call.

⚠️ If the call is refused:
The message says so plainly, and distinguishes two cases: a transient failure (retrying makes sense) and a refusal from the carrier — unverified source number, exhausted credit — where retrying changes nothing until it is fixed on their side.

🔎 The facts, too: the debrief also lists the concrete findings the call produced — opening hours, availability, the answer you were waiting for — even when nothing needs doing afterwards.

q14.question: Can LIA accept a date or an extra charge proposed during the call?
q14.answer: No, never automatically. The call summary first shows what the other party actually proposed — date, place, extra cost, pending decision — then, separately, the possible follow-ups: create a reminder, make a commitment, plan a meeting. Each one prepares the message in the composer instead of sending it, and every action that writes externally keeps its own confirmation prompt. No path turns “the other party proposed X” into “you accepted X”.

peers.title: Connections between users
peers.description: Connect with other users of this LIA instance, relay messages assistant-to-assistant, and open chosen read-only shares.

q1.question: How do I connect with someone?
q1.answer: Both of you enable discovery in Settings → Connections (off by default), then one searches the other's exact full name — your own searchable name is shown in the section with a copy button. Send a request (with an optional note); the other person accepts or declines in one click, from the chat card or the settings. A masked email fragment (j…@g….com) helps tell homonyms apart. Nothing else is shared by connecting.

q2.question: How do I send a message to a connection?
q2.answer: Just tell LIA: tell Marie I am running late. You see a confirmation card with the exact wording before anything leaves. The message is then delivered by the recipient's own assistant, in its personality and language, which names you as the sender — and your assistant confirms delivery in your chat. Replying works the same way: a reply is simply a new relayed message. The small AI cost of delivery is billed to the sender, and daily quotas prevent abuse. Relayed messages have a length limit (2,000 characters by default): if yours is too long, LIA tells you the exact length and the limit, and offers to shorten or summarize it — nothing is sent without you knowing.

q3.question: What can I share, and what does the other person see?
q3.answer: Per connection, you choose read-only shares: calendar as free/busy only or with event titles, and task titles. Nothing is shared by default. Both directions are visible to both sides in the Connections section, every access is re-checked at the moment of the read, and recorded in an access log you can consult. You can change or revoke a share at any time. When you ask is Marie free tomorrow at 10?, LIA reads the calendar Marie chose as her default — not an arbitrary one — and gives you the hours on your own clock. All-day entries (a birthday, a reminder) are listed apart from real meetings, so they never make someone look busy all day.

q4.question: How do I block someone, and what do they notice?
q4.answer: Block from the chat (under a relayed message) or from the Connections section, with a confirmation. Blocking ends the connection silently: the other person is not notified, can no longer find you in discovery, and any message they try to relay quietly goes nowhere. Unblocking does not restore anything — you would have to reconnect explicitly.

q5.question: Can someone find me without my consent?
q5.answer: No. Discovery is opt-in and off by default. Search only matches your exact full name (accents and case are forgiven, but there is no partial or fuzzy search), and without a full name on your profile you are unfindable. Blocked, unknown and declined targets all receive the exact same neutral answer, so nobody can probe whether you exist, declined, or blocked them.

q6.question: What happens when I remove a connection, or delete my account?
q6.answer: Removing a connection ends all shares immediately, and both assistants inform their users. Relayed message content is scrubbed after delivery — LIA does not keep a browsable message history. Your GDPR export includes your connections and shares, and deleting your account purges both sides of every pair.

relations.title: Relations (personal CRM)
relations.description: The Relations page: everything LIA knows about the people you deal with, favorites included.

q1.question: What is the Relations page?
q1.answer: Open Relations in the navigation bar: one card per person, aggregating what LIA already tracks — open commitments, phone calls, memories that mention them and relayed messages. Opening a card shows the 360° sheet, whose first section is where you launch a 360° recap in the chat. It is a lens over existing data: nothing new is collected.

q2.question: How do favorites work?
q2.answer: Tap the star on any card (or in the 360° sheet) — no need to open anything. Favorites keep their own band at the top of the page, and a starred person never disappears, even when there has been no interaction for a long while. Tap the star again to unstar; with many relations, use the name filter that appears above the list.

q3.question: What is the small LIA badge on some cards?
q3.answer: It marks relations who are also connected users of your LIA instance (see the Connections section). The badge is read-only and only appears when the connections feature is enabled — a bridge between your personal CRM and assistant-to-assistant connections.

q4.question: Why does a card say the match is best-effort?
q4.answer: People are grouped by name, with accents and case forgiven. When the spellings differ across sources, or when a memory merely mentions a common first name, LIA says the match is best-effort rather than pretending to be sure — honesty over false precision.

q5.question: What does a relationship card show?
q5.answer: Beyond what LIA tracks itself, the card shows what your connected accounts know about that person: their address-book entry (nickname, job title, birthday, postal addresses, relations, links…), the mail exchanged and the meetings shared. Those three are found by email address, resolved from the contact card — with no address on file, LIA says so instead of pretending it found nothing. They state the window they looked at rather than a total a provider page cannot prove, and each carries a refresh control.

q6.question: How do I choose what LIA reads for a 360° recap?
q6.answer: The first section of the card, 360° recap, holds the checkboxes: which sources to use (contact card, commitments, memories, calls, relayed messages, mail, meetings), the direction of exchanges (received, sent), the role in meetings (attendee, organizer) and how many items each section may contribute. Your choice is saved before the chat opens, so LIA applies it instead of guessing it from your sentence — and it pre-fills next time. Clearing everything is not the same as taking everything: an unticked source is simply not read.

q7.question: Why did a connected person have no mail and no meetings?
q7.answer: Exchanges are found by address, not by name: someone you never saved in your address book had none, so there was nothing to match. If that person is a connected user and has turned on address sharing (Connections setting), LIA now uses it to find, in your mail and your calendar, the exchanges and meetings they appear in. Without that sharing nothing changes: their setting stays the only thing that decides. And if no meeting involves them, the section stays empty — LIA does not fill the silence with an event of your calendar they neither organise nor attend.

q8.question: How do I merge two cards that are the same person?
q8.answer: LIA groups what is written the same, accents and capitals aside. It cannot guess that a raw phone number and a name are one relationship, or that "Dad" is "John Smith": that is a judgement, and only you can make it. Open the card you want to keep, scroll to Group relationships, pick the other card and confirm. The merge is reversible: it appears on the card with its own undo, and nothing is rewritten in your sources — both cards come back exactly as they were. It never changes the directory of connected people: a display grouping must not be able to redirect a message to another account.

q9.question: Can I ask about my calls or my commitments with someone?
q9.answer: Yes. "When did I last call Marie?", "what do I owe her?", "what did we pass on through LIA?" now get an answer. Before, a question about a call could produce a plan to phone her and ask: the telephony domain only knew how to place calls, so covering its own domain meant acting. LIA now reads your past calls, your open commitments and the relayed messages, through exactly the same computation as the relationship card — so the assistant and the card cannot give you two different answers. The total count is always exact, next to the page shown.

q10.question: Can I act on a commitment from a person's card?
q10.answer:
Yes. A relationship's card lists the open commitments with that person — what you owe them, what you are waiting for — and offers four gestures on each: Done, Follow up (opens the chat with a message already written, without sending it), No longer relevant and Correct.

The correction covers the wording and the deadline. The ledger fills itself from your conversations, so it sometimes mishears a sentence, or reads "by Friday" as the wrong Friday. The other party and the meaning cannot be edited: changing those would describe a different commitment rather than correct this one.

The same gestures live in Settings → Features → "Commitments", which lists them all, across every person.

tool_examples_services.title: Email, Calendar & Contacts Examples
tool_examples_services.description: How to use your connected services (Google, Apple iCloud or Microsoft 365): emails, contacts, calendar, Drive and Tasks

q1.question: How do I search my contacts?
q1.answer:
Google Contacts - Talk naturally to LIA:

🔍 Simple search:
• "Find John's contact"
• "Show me Mary Smith's phone number"
• "What's Peter's email?"

🔍 Advanced search:
• "Find all contacts at Acme Corp"
• "Search for contacts with a number starting with 555"
• "List my contacts in New York"

📋 Results display:
LIA displays a card for each contact with name, photo, phones, emails and organization. Photos are clickable and display larger (2x zoom) in a modal window.

💡 Tip:
You can then say "the first one" or "the one from company X" to reference a contact.

q2.question: How do I create or modify a contact?
q2.answer:
Google Contacts - Creation and modification:

➕ Create a contact:
• "Create a contact for John Smith, email john@example.com, phone 555-123-4567"
• "Add a new contact: Dr. Martin, medical office, 555-987-6543"

✏️ Modify a contact:
• "Update Mary's number to 555-111-2222"
• "Add address 10 Main Street to Peter's contact"
• "Change John's email to john.new@example.com"

🗑️ Delete a contact:
• "Delete the contact Jane Doe"

⚠️ Approval required:
For any modification, LIA shows you a preview and asks for confirmation before executing.

q3.question: How do I search my emails?
q3.answer:
Gmail - Powerful search:

🔍 Simple search:
• "Show my unread emails"
• "Find emails from Amazon"
• "Emails from this week"

🔍 Advanced search:
• "Emails from Peter about the budget"
• "Emails with PDF attachments"
• "Emails sent last month"
• "Important unread emails"

📂 By folder:
• "Emails in my inbox"
• "My sent emails"
• "Emails in the Work folder"

📋 Results:
LIA displays a card per email with sender, subject, date and preview.

💡 By default:
LIA searches ALL your emails (not just inbox) for complete results.

q4.question: How do I read an email in detail?
q4.answer:
Gmail - Full content display:

📖 After a search:
• "Show me the first email"
• "Read Peter's email"
• "Display the content of the second one"

📖 Direct access:
• "Open the last email from Amazon"
• "Show the content of the email about the invoice"

📋 What you'll see:
• Sender and recipients
• Date and time
• Full subject
• Message body (text and HTML)
• List of attachments
• Link to open in Gmail

💡 Navigation:
After reading an email, you can say "reply to this email" or "forward it to Mary".

q5.question: How do I send an email?
q5.answer:
Gmail - Sending emails with preview:

📤 Simple send:
• "Send an email to john@example.com: Hello, I confirm our appointment tomorrow."

📤 Structured send:
• "Send an email to mary@example.com with subject 'Project meeting' and content: Hello Mary, can you confirm your availability for Friday's meeting?"

📤 With CC:
• "Send an email to peter@example.com CC john@example.com about the monthly report"

✅ Sending process:
1. LIA generates a draft
2. You see the complete preview (recipient, subject, content)
3. You can approve, modify or cancel
4. The email is sent only after your approval

⚠️ Security tip:
Always verify the recipient's email address in the preview!

q6.question: How do I reply to or forward an email?
q6.answer:
Gmail - Reply and forward:

↩️ Reply:
• "Reply to Peter's last email: Thanks, noted!"
• "Reply to the email about the invoice to confirm payment"
• "Reply all to John's email"

↪️ Forward:
• "Forward the Amazon email to accounting@company.com"
• "Forward the second email to Mary with the message: FYI"

📋 Preview before sending:
• You see the complete draft
• The thread is preserved
• Attachments are included (forward)

💡 Tip:
After a search, use references like "the first one", "John's one" to designate the email.

q7.question: How do I delete an email?
q7.answer:
Gmail - Secure deletion:

🗑️ Delete an email:
• "Delete the spam email from yesterday"
• "Move the first email to trash"
• "Delete the promotional email from this morning"

⚠️ Secure process:
1. LIA shows you the email to be deleted
2. You see the sender, subject and date
3. Confirmation required before deletion
4. The email is moved to trash (not permanently deleted)

♻️ Recovery possible:
Emails in trash are kept for 30 days by Gmail before permanent deletion.

💡 Tip:
To permanently delete, you must do it directly in Gmail.

q8.question: How do I view my calendar events?
q8.answer:
Google Calendar - Schedule consultation:

📅 Daily view:
• "What do I have scheduled today?"
• "My appointments for tomorrow"
• "Schedule for January 15"

📅 Weekly view:
• "Show my week"
• "What do I have planned next week?"
• "My meetings this week"

🔍 Specific search:
• "Find meetings with Sophie"
• "When is my next doctor's appointment?"
• "Events at the office this week"

📋 Information displayed:
• Event title
• Date and time
• Location (if defined)
• Participants
• Link to open in Google Calendar

q9.question: How do I create a calendar event?
q9.answer:
Google Calendar - Event creation:

➕ Simple creation:
• "Create an appointment tomorrow at 2pm"
• "Schedule a meeting Monday at 10am"

➕ Detailed creation:
• "Create an event 'Project meeting' tomorrow from 2pm to 4pm in room A"
• "Schedule lunch with John on Friday noon at The Bistro restaurant"

➕ With participants:
• "Create a meeting tomorrow at 2pm with peter@example.com and mary@example.com"

✅ Creation process:
1. LIA generates a draft of the event
2. You see all details (date, time, location, participants)
3. You can modify or approve
4. The event is created after your confirmation

💡 Tip:
Set your default calendar in settings so you don't have to specify it each time.

q10.question: How do I modify or delete an event?
q10.answer:
Google Calendar - Modification and deletion:

✏️ Modify an event:
• "Move my 3pm meeting to 4pm"
• "Change tomorrow's meeting location to room B"
• "Add Mary as a participant to Monday's meeting"
• "Extend the meeting by one hour"

🗑️ Delete an event:
• "Cancel tomorrow's meeting"
• "Delete the appointment with Dr. Martin"
• "Cancel all my events on Friday"

⚠️ Approval required:
Any modification or deletion requires your explicit confirmation.

📧 Notifications:
If the event has participants, they will be automatically notified of changes by Google Calendar.

q11.question: How do I search my Google Drive files?
q11.answer:
Google Drive - Exploring your files:

🔍 Search by name:
• "Find the budget file"
• "Search for the Q3 report document"
• "Where is the meeting notes file?"

🔍 Search by type:
• "Show my PDF files"
• "List spreadsheets in my Drive"
• "Find presentations"

🔍 Search by date/sharing:
• "Files modified this week"
• "Documents shared by Mary"
• "My recent files"

📋 Results:
LIA displays the name, type, size and modification date of each file, with a link to open it in Drive.

💡 Then:
Say "open the first one" or "read the report content" to access the file.

q12.question: How do I read a Drive file?
q12.answer:
Google Drive - Reading content:

📖 Read a document:
• "Open the Q3 report document"
• "Show me the content of the notes file"
• "Read the first file"

📊 Supported file types:
• 📄 Text documents (Google Docs, .txt, .docx)
• 📊 Spreadsheets (Google Sheets, .xlsx) - structure preserved
• 📽️ Presentations (Google Slides, .pptx) - slide text
• 📝 Plain text files

⚠️ Limitations:
• Images and graphics are not displayed (text only)
• Very large files may be truncated
• Binary files (videos, zip) are not readable

💡 Tip:
For complex files, ask for a summary: "Summarize the report content"

q13.question: How do I manage my tasks?
q13.answer:
Google Tasks / Microsoft To Do - Task management:

📋 View tasks:
• "Show my tasks"
• "What do I have to do?"
• "List my current tasks"

➕ Create a task:
• "Add a task: call the bank"
• "Create a task 'Prepare the presentation' for Friday"
• "Remind me to send the report tomorrow"

✅ Complete a task:
• "Mark the 'call the bank' task as done"
• "I finished the first task"

📝 Task lists:
• "Show my task lists"
• "Tasks from the Projects list"
• "Create a task in the Shopping list"

💡 Tip:
Set your default task list in settings to save time. Commands are the same regardless of whether you use Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do — LIA automatically uses the active provider.

q14.question: What is the draft and approval system?
q14.answer:
